title: ProjectInfo: lucide icons per metadata + 4-column layout (5x4 instead of 10x2)
description:
ProjectInfo currently renders metadata as a 10-row × 2-column dl (Key/BPM/Sig/Sample rate/Frame rate/Tracks/Created/Modified/Bundle size/Audio files, sometimes Impulse responses). Two changes:

## 1. Lucide icon per row

Add a small Lucide icon next to each metadata label so users scan the grid by glyph rather than reading every label. Keep icons monochrome (currentColor) and tied to the label semantically:

- **Key** → `Music`
- **BPM** → `Activity` (heartbeat) or `Gauge`
- **Time signature** → `Clock4` or `Hourglass`
- **Sample rate** → `Waveform` (or `AudioLines`)
- **Frame rate** → `Film`
- **Tracks** → `Layers`
- **Created** → `Calendar`
- **Modified** → `RotateCw` or `History`
- **Bundle size** → `HardDrive` (or `Package`)
- **Audio files** → `FileAudio`
- **Impulse responses** → `Radio` (or `Speaker`)

(Final icon picks are the implementer's call — these are starting points.)

## 2. 5×4 layout instead of 10×2

Today: a 10-row × 2-col `<dl>` (label / value, label / value, …). Convert to a 4-column grid where each visual row carries TWO label/value pairs side by side, halving vertical real estate. Roughly 5 rows × 4 cols (icon-label | value | icon-label | value).

Implementation hint: switch from `<dl>` to a CSS grid container with `grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto 1fr` (or similar). Pair items 0+1, 2+3, etc. into single rows.

## Acceptance

- Each metadata item has a distinct Lucide icon next to its label.
- The grid renders with two label/value pairs per row.
- Total vertical height for the section is roughly half what it is today on a typical project.
- Icons are accessible — either decorative (`aria-hidden`) with the label carrying the meaning, or labelled appropriately.
- Existing ProjectInfo tests still pass (asserting on the rendered values).

## Out of scope

- Hoisting Key · BPM · Sig into the project header — that's a separate PM-review item, file as its own bead if needed.
- Animated/interactive icons (hover tooltips beyond the existing label).
close_reason: Shipped: ProjectInfo metadata grid gains a Lucide icon per row (Music/Activity/Clock4/AudioLines/Film/Layers/Calendar/History/HardDrive/FileAudio/Radio) and switches from 2-col dl (10x2) to a 4-col grid that auto-flows pairs side by side. Halves vertical real estate. Reflows to 2-col under 720px so narrow widths don't squeeze pairs. 296 tests pass (1 new). Existing value-format tests still pass — the rendered values didn't change.

title: Cmd-+ / Cmd-- / Cmd-0 text zoom with persistence
description:
Add accessibility-friendly text zoom controlled by macOS keyboard conventions:

- **Cmd +**  → increase font size (e.g. +10% per press, capped at +200%)
- **Cmd -**  → decrease font size (capped at -50%)
- **Cmd 0**  → reset to 100% (default)

Setting persists across launches via the existing `@tauri-apps/plugin-store` mechanism (used today for recent projects in src/lib/persistence.ts).

## Implementation hints

- Centralise the scale factor on the `<html>` or `<body>` root via a CSS custom property (`--zoom`) and multiply font-size on tokenised text. Most components already use `var(--fs-*)` tokens, so a single root-level scale should propagate cleanly.
- New `useUIStore` slice: `textZoom: number` (default 1.0), `setTextZoom(n)`, `bumpZoom(delta)`, `resetZoom()`.
- Keyboard handler in App.tsx (top-level) listens for the three combinations. macOS uses metaKey for Cmd; check `event.metaKey && event.key === '='` (the '+' shows as '=' without shift on most layouts), `=== '-'`, `=== '0'`.
- Persist via the same store-plugin pattern as recent projects; load on mount, write on change.

## Acceptance

- Cmd-+ scales the app's text up; Cmd-- scales it down; Cmd-0 resets.
- Setting persists across app restarts.
- Zoom level reaches sensible bounds (e.g. 0.75x – 2.0x) and saturates rather than continuing forever.
- Existing layout tolerates the zoom range — no clipped sections at 1.5x.

## Out of scope

- Zoom for the WebView itself (browser-level Cmd-+ would zoom everything including the title bar) — we want app-level text zoom, not WebView zoom.
- Per-section font controls — one global zoom only.
close_reason: Text zoom shipped. ui-store gains textZoom + setTextZoom/bumpTextZoom/resetTextZoom (clamped [0.75, 2.0]); tokens.css wraps every --fs-* in calc(N * var(--text-zoom)); App.tsx listens for Cmd-+/-/= /-/_/0 (handles unshifted '=' as '+' on US layouts) and persists the value via lib/persistence.ts loadTextZoom/persistTextZoom. 295 tests pass (12 new across ui-store + persistence). Spacing tokens unchanged — only text scales.

title: npm run bump — sync version across package.json, tauri.conf.json, Cargo.toml
description:
Reuse the versioning setup from `/Users/rhyd/code/flowcus-v2`:

- `scripts/sync-version.js` reads package.json's version and writes it to:
  - `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (key `version`)

  - `\"bump\": \"npm version patch\"` (flowcus-v2's bump also force-adds Sparkle binaries — skip that block until lpx-explorer adopts Sparkle, see lpx-explorer-snx)

## Acceptance

- Running `npm run bump` on a clean tree leaves the working tree clean afterwards (commit + tag are made).
- `scripts/sync-version.js` ports the flowcus-v2 logic verbatim minus the Sparkle git-add block.

## Out of scope

- Sparkle / auto-updater wiring — see lpx-explorer-snx.
- Release branch / tag-push automation — manual `git push --tags` for now.

Wired as the npm version lifecycle hook with preversion=quality. Verified end-to-end: simulated bump 0.0.0→0.0.1 propagated to all three files cleanly. Revisit Sparkle binary auto-add when lpx-explorer-snx lands.

title: Renamed-but-unrecorded audio tracks: locate user-given name in ProjectData binary section (NOT bplists)
description:
Spawned from lpx-explorer-3iv spike (2026-05-06). The bplist parser approach proposed by lpx-explorer-14d was disproven — see the spike comment on 14d. Track names are NOT in NSKeyedArchive blobs; they live somewhere in the binary section of `ProjectData`.

## What is still missing

Audio tracks the user has renamed but never recorded into render as `"Audio N"` instead of their user-given name. Coverage so far:

- Audio tracks WITH recorded regions: name recovered from cluster_regions (lpx-explorer-qib).
- Instrument tracks: name falls back to the loaded AU display name (lpx-explorer-59o).
- **Renamed but unrecorded audio tracks**: still `"Audio N"`. THIS BEAD.

The Python tool also shows `"Audio N"` for these tracks — the format is not reverse-engineered there either.

## Where to look (binary section, not bplists)

Spike confirmed bplists do not contain user-given track names. Re-investigate the binary section of `ProjectData`. Hypotheses worth testing:

1. The channel-strip record itself carries an inline name field today's parser doesn't read. Check the bytes immediately following each strip ID for an ASCII or UTF-16 string before the next 4CC anchor.
2. There's an unidentified record signature (analogous to `OCuA`/`gRuA`/`karT`) that maps strip-id → display-name. Run the existing 4CC scanner across `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx` and look for ASCII-printable 4-byte sequences that aren't currently handled.
3. The name lives in `DisplayState.plist` (a sibling file in the bundle, not `ProjectData`). Check whether opening that file as a regular plist surfaces the renames.

Repro project: `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx`. Logic ground truth (6 tracks) is in lpx-explorer-14d Notes. The two `Untitled` tracks are likely actually-named-Untitled in Logic, so the failing case to chase is whether any *other* renamed audio track surfaces correctly today and which doesn't. Pick a fresh repro project where the user has renamed an audio track, never armed it, never recorded — that's the minimal case.

## Out of scope

Apple stock plug-in coverage — that's a separate gap with the same root cause (bplists don't help) but a different solution. Tracked separately. Channel-routing, plug-in slot assignments, region positions are also out of scope.

## Acceptance criteria

Audio tracks renamed but never recorded into render their user-given name in `<TrackList>` on a fresh repro project; cargo tests cover the byte-level extraction; `lpx-toolkit/CLAUDE.md` updated to document where the name lives.
acceptance_criteria: Audio tracks renamed but never recorded into render their user-given name in <TrackList> on a fresh repro project; cargo tests cover the byte-level extraction; lpx-toolkit/CLAUDE.md updated to document where the name lives.
close_reason: Two-line whitelist fix in tracks_registry.rs — added instrument signatures 0xda 0x11 (Apple stock-instrument tracks like Bass) and 0xe7 0x10 (Alchemy / sampler tracks). On the repro project this recovers 5/6 user tracks (was 3): Piano, Bass, Drums, Luscious Arp Layers, UnexpectedlyNamedTrack. The 6th is genuinely-named-Untitled — correctly filtered as REGISTRY_NOISE. Wired through the existing tracks_registry path; <TrackRegistry> component already displayed these. Also fixed misleading 'lives in NSKeyedArchive blobs' comment in <TrackRegistry> (premise disproven by lpx-explorer-3iv). lpx-toolkit/CLAUDE.md updated with the two new signatures.

comments.text:
# Reverse-engineering lead (2026-05-06)

User experiment: rename one `Untitled` audio track in `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx` to `UnexpectedlyNamedTrack`. ProjectData grew from 1,061,235 to 1,095,298 bytes after Logic rewrote it. The new name appears EXACTLY ONCE in the binary section, at 0xF9A7A. That single occurrence is the canonical track-name slot.

## Pattern A — track-name record signature

Byte context around the unique `UnexpectedlyNamedTrack` occurrence:

```
0xF9A2A: 01 11 a1 01 19 00 40 00 f0 01 04 00 00 00 00 00   ← record start (~80 bytes before name)
0xF9A3A: 40 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
0xF9A4A: 00 00 08 07 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
0xF9A5A: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00
0xF9A6A: 00 00 00 00 22 12 00 00 00 00 80 13 00 00 16 00   ← last 2 bytes = uint16 LE length
0xF9A7A: U n e x p e c t e d l y N a m e d T r a c k        (length 0x0016 = 22 ✓)
0xF9A8A: 64 54 72 61 63 6b 0e 00 00 ff 00 01 00 00 00 00
```

Identical 16-byte fingerprint `40 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 / 00 00 08 07 00 00 00 00` at offset -64..-40 from the string also appears at:
- 0xF9288 (`Luscious Arp Layers`, length 0x0013 = 19) ← Track 4 canonical slot
- 0xF987F (`Untitled`, length 0x0008 = 8)            ← canonical slot for one of the unnamed tracks

The 4 OTHER occurrences of `Luscious Arp Layers` in ProjectData are NOT track-name slots:

| # | Offset | Context | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0x31846 | `Luscious Arp Layers.acp` | Sampler-patch filename |
| 2 | 0x3190D | `<alchemypreset>...Name = Luscious Arp Layers...` | Alchemy preset XML inside plug-in state |
| 3 | **0xF9288** | **Pattern A signature** | **Canonical track-name slot** |
| 4 | 0xFBE1A | `qeSM` (4CC `MSeq` reversed) | Region/sequence record referencing track |
| 5 | 0x10038A | `qeSM` again | Another sequence record |

## Implementation strategy

1. Scan ProjectData for the 16-byte signature `40 00 00 00 (×8 zeros) 00 00 08 07 00 00 00 00`.
2. Skip forward through trailing zero-padding to the uint16 length-prefix immediately before the next non-zero region.
3. Read uint16 LE length, read that many ASCII bytes — that's the user-given track name.
4. Cross-reference with `find_tracks` via the existing offset-proximity heuristic (`assign_user_names`).

Note: confirm whether the existing `find_tracks` / `tracks_registry` Rust modules already identify these record boundaries — they may already detect the channel-strip record and just need a name-extraction call within it.

## Test fixture strategy

Hand-build a `ProjectData`-shaped fixture with two records: one with the Pattern A signature + a known name, and one with a `qeSM`-style region record containing the same string (negative case — must NOT extract). No real Logic data needed — the signature is small enough to fixture from scratch.

## Verification target

Re-run the parser on `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx` after implementation:
- The renamed audio track now displays `UnexpectedlyNamedTrack` instead of `Audio N`.
- The two `Untitled` tracks still display `Untitled` (genuine).
- The Bass / Piano / Drums / Luscious Arp Layers tracks unchanged.
- No regression on tracks recovered via cluster_regions or AU display name fallback.

## Related diagnostic scripts

Throwaway in `/tmp/`: `locate_strings.py`, `track_anchor.py`. Output at `/tmp/track_anchor.out`. Both reuse `lpx_inspect.extract_bplists` from lpx-toolkit. Discard after this comment lands.

title: Re-enable LibraryHome tile view + diagnose post-hydrate render hang
description:
## Background

After lpx-explorer-1di (tile view) and lpx-explorer-3mo (auto-add ~/Music/Logic) shipped, the app started showing a blank window after a clean cold-start hydration:

```
[+0ms]    [main] start
[+15419ms] [html] inline script ran    ← vite cold-start; expected
[+15744ms] [bridge] installed
[+15782ms] [hydrate] complete           ← clean
... blank window forever ...
```

JS reaches `[hydrate] complete` cleanly, no errors logged via the dev-log bridge, but React never paints / never becomes interactive (right-click context menu doesn't open either, suggesting webview event loop is starved).

LibraryHome was the most likely contributor — it mounts a tile per project, each tile calls `useLibrarySummariesStore.getOrParse` in a useEffect, parses fan out under the concurrency cap. Some interaction in that path (effect chain, render loop, IPC bridge backpressure) seems to lock the renderer.

## Triage state (current)

- App.tsx unconditionally renders EmptyState when status is idle (1di disabled)
- Auto-select-for-browse on hydrate is disabled
- The `[render] App` console breadcrumb is still in place
- Folder persistence (vn5), back-button (vrt), concurrency cap (bh4), and other stores all stay shipped

## Investigation steps

1. With 1di disabled, confirm the user can interact normally (rail clicks, project open, etc.).
2. Re-enable LibraryHome incrementally to bisect the cause:
   - First: render `<LibraryHome />` with empty `folder.projects` (no tiles). Confirm hang or no.
   - Then: render with 5 tiles. Confirm.
   - Then: 50, 200.
3. If the hang correlates with tile count, the cause is likely in `LibraryHomeTile`'s mount effect or in `useLibrarySummariesStore`'s slot-queue interactions with React batching.
4. Watch the `[render] App` breadcrumb — if it stops while `[parse]` keeps coming, the renderer is suspended; if both stop, the JS event loop itself is jammed.

## Likely suspects (in order)

1. **Render storm during cap queue drain.** Each `getOrParse` resolution triggers a Zustand `set()` → all subscribers re-render. With 200 tiles, that's 200 store mutations cascading.
2. **Effect double-fire under StrictMode.** Each tile's useEffect fires twice in dev. The slot queue might be over-subscribed and not resolving deterministically.
3. **IPC bridge saturation.** Each parse logs via `console.info` which forwards via `invoke('log_event')`. With 200 parses each emitting 3+ logs, the IPC bridge could backpressure.

## Acceptance

- LibraryHome re-enabled with no render hang on a 200+ project library
- App responds to right-click (context menu opens) within 100ms even mid-parse
- Triage code (App.tsx void/comment markers, [render] App breadcrumb) cleaned up
close_reason: Resolved without code changes. Root cause was environmental — macOS WebKit / GPU state across multiple Tauri apps (Flowcus had the same blank-screen symptom). A Mac restart cleared it. <LibraryHome /> was re-enabled and the auto-select-on-hydrate restored in commit fd53d27 with no regressions; subsequent fixes (auto-add persistence df3e179, failed-projects list 81acc67, error-shape unpack 028d015) brought the tile-view flow back online and shipped end-to-end.

title: Persist active library folders across launches
description:
## Problem

Discovered after lpx-explorer-3mo shipped. The first-launch auto-add of `~/Music/Logic` works, but on the SECOND launch the folder is gone — the user has to manually re-open it via File > Open Recent Folder.

Cause: `useLibraryStore.folders` is in-memory only. The persistence pipeline (`lib/persistence.ts`) saves `recent` (project paths) and `recentFolders` (paths the File menu lists) but NOT `folders` (the active rail list with scan state). On relaunch, the auto-add gate is closed because `recent.length > 0` from any opened project, and folders is empty so no tile grid renders.

## Proposed fix

Persist the active `folders` list as a flat array of paths. On launch, hydrate by calling `addFolder` for each persisted path — re-triggers `scan_folder` so the projects array is fresh, but the folder appears in the rail immediately.

Implementation:

1. New `KEY_FOLDERS` key in `lib/persistence.ts` storing `string[]` of folder paths.
2. New `loadPersistedFolderPaths()` and `persistFolderPaths(paths)` helpers.
3. `App.tsx` hydration effect: after `useLibraryStore.hydrate(persisted)`, call `addFolder(path)` for each persisted folder path that isn't already there. (`addFolder` is already idempotent on path collision.)
4. `App.tsx` subscription effect: when `state.folders` changes, persist the new paths.

The auto-add still gates on `recent.length === 0 && recentFolders.length === 0` — meaning if the user removes the auto-added `~/Music/Logic`, it doesn't come back on next launch (recentFolders preserves the path even after folder removal, closing the gate).

## Acceptance

- After auto-add of ~/Music/Logic on first launch, relaunching the app shows ~/Music/Logic still in the LibraryRail without manual intervention.
- Removing a folder from the rail keeps it removed across relaunches.
- A folder added via "Open folder" persists across relaunches the same way.
- A scanFolder re-runs on hydration so project lists are fresh (catches new .logicx files added since last quit).
- Test: store-set folders, re-mount App, assert addFolder gets called for each persisted path.
close_reason: Active folders now persist across launches. New KEY_FOLDERS in tauri-plugin-store; load/persist helpers in lib/persistence.ts; App.tsx hydrates folders on mount (re-running scan_folder so project lists are fresh) and persists on change. Hydration effect refactored to keep cognitive complexity under budget. 337 tests pass (5 new on persistence helpers).

title: Library home: concurrency-limited parse + progress indicator (no more beachball)
description:
## Problem

After lpx-explorer-1di + lpx-explorer-3mo shipped, first launch on a real ~/Music/Logic with 100+ projects shows the macOS beachball during startup. Two compounding causes:

1. **Parse fan-out.** Every tile in `<LibraryHome />` mounts simultaneously and calls `useLibrarySummariesStore.getOrParse(path)`. With N projects, N concurrent Tauri `parse_project` invocations fire on the same frame — flooding the IPC bridge and blocking the renderer while React processes the resulting cascade of store updates.
2. **No progress feedback.** `<LibraryHome />` shows a generic 'Scanning folder…' line while the folder scan runs but no count, and once the scan finishes the header switches to silent — even though dozens of tile parses are still pending. The user sees an unresponsive grid of skeleton tiles with no signal that work is happening.

## Proposed fix

Three changes, all small:

1. **Concurrency cap in `useLibrarySummariesStore`.** Limit to 4 in-flight `parseProject` calls; queue the rest. Drains naturally as parses complete. Same dedup semantics as today (cache hits + concurrent calls for the same path collapse).
2. **Defer per-tile parse kickoff.** `<LibraryHomeTile />` schedules `getOrParse` via `requestIdleCallback` (with a `setTimeout(0)` fallback) so React paints first; parses fan out on the next idle frame instead of competing with the initial render.
3. **Progress line in `<LibraryHome />` header.** When a scan is running OR tiles are still parsing, show:
   - During scan: `Scanning folder… 47 found`
   - After scan, while tiles parse: `Parsing 12 of 47`
   - When everything's done: nothing (just the header).

## Out of scope

- IntersectionObserver virtualisation (a v2 optimisation; cap + idle-defer already buys most of the win).
- Per-tile parse cancellation (no UX flow today that needs it).
- Cross-folder progress aggregation (one folder at a time).

## Acceptance

- First launch on a 200+ project library doesn't freeze the UI thread (no beachball; clicking buttons during the parse-storm responds in <100ms).
- LibraryHome header shows a live progress count during scan AND during the parse-storm that follows.
- Summary cache reaches the same final state regardless of concurrency cap.
- Tests cover: cap behaviour (5 calls → max 4 in flight at once); progress derivation when summaries partially populate.
close_reason: Concurrency cap + progress indicator shipped. PARSE_CONCURRENCY=4 in useLibrarySummariesStore prevents the parse fan-out that was freezing the UI thread; LibraryHome header shows live 'Scanning… N found' / 'Reading X of N…' with a determinate progress bar. 329 tests pass.

title: Library home view — project tiles for the active folder
description:
The Python tool's `--serve` view ships a project-tile grid on its index page (`.proj-card` in `lpx_inspect.py`) — each card surfaces key / BPM / time-sig / dates / size / track-count chips. LPX Explorer has no equivalent: the main area is either EmptyState (no project) or ProjectInspector (one project loaded). When the user has a library folder picked but no specific project chosen, there's a useful third state we currently don't render.

## Problem

The user lands on the app, picks a folder of projects, and… has to either click each project in the rail one by one or scroll the rail to find one. They've lost the at-a-glance browsability that Logic-Pro-itself doesn't even have.

## Proposed UX (locked)

A new **library-browse** state in the main area, triggered when:
- A library folder is *selected* (active) in LibraryRail, AND
- No specific project is loaded (`projectStore.current.kind === 'idle'`)

The main area renders a responsive tile grid of every `.logicx` in that folder. Each tile shows:

- **Project name** (top, large)
- **Key · BPM · Time sig** (one inline line, the musically meaningful triplet)
- **Tracks · Plug-ins** (count badges, secondary tone)
- **Modified** (relative, e.g. '3 days ago')
- **Size** (right-aligned, tabular)

Click a tile → opens that project (existing `openProject` flow). Hovering a tile shows the full path as a title attribute.

## Data dependencies (shared with lpx-explorer-185)

Each tile needs a `ProjectSummary` for its `.logicx`. Two strategies:

- **Lazy on visibility** — parse via `IntersectionObserver` when a tile scrolls into view; show a skeleton tile until it resolves. Spreads cost; first scroll is jankier.
- **Lazy on render** — parse all visible-folder projects when the library-browse state mounts; rate-limit a worker pool to avoid hammering the FS.

→ **IntersectionObserver lazy** for v1. Same `useLibrarySummariesStore` cache that lpx-explorer-185 needs. File the cache as a child bead first; this bead consumes it.

## States to render

- **Loading** — skeleton tiles while a folder is being scanned (folder.status === 'scanning').
- **Empty** — 'No `.logicx` projects in this folder.' (existing copy from FolderNode).
- **Loaded** — the tile grid.
- **Per-tile** — skeleton until that project's summary resolves; final once parsed.
- **Per-tile error** — the tile shows project name + a quiet 'couldn't read' line; click still attempts open.

## Implementation hints

- New component `src/components/Library/LibraryHome.tsx` rendered from `App.tsx`'s main slot when the library-browse state predicate matches.
- New ui-store slice: `selectedLibraryFolder: string | null` (in-session). LibraryRail folders become clickable headers that toggle this. Currently FolderNode's header expands the rail tree; clicking the header would BOTH expand the tree AND set the folder as the active library-browse target.
- Tile grid via CSS grid with `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(220px, 1fr))`.
- Per-tile parse: invoke `parse_project` (Tauri command exists) when the tile intersects.

## Out of scope

- **Search / filter within tiles** — LibraryRail's existing search already narrows the set that flows into the tile grid. Sort options (chronological / alphabetical / by size) deferred to a v2 bead.
- **Drag-to-reorder** — Logic doesn't surface project ordering; we don't either.
- **Tile thumbnails** (waveform / artwork) — Logic has no canonical thumbnail; rendering one is expensive parser work.
- **Cross-folder rollup** — that's lpx-explorer-185. The library-browse view shows ONE folder at a time.
- **Per-tile actions** (copy path, reveal in finder, etc.) — defer; click-to-open is enough for v1.

## Relationship to other beads

- **Depends on** the per-project-summary cache child bead from `lpx-explorer-185`. File 185's decomposition first; mark this bead's first child as `bd dep add <this> <185-cache-child>` once that exists.
- **Synergy with** `lpx-explorer-3mo` (auto-add ~/Music/Logic). Once that ships, the first launch lands on this tile grid automatically — a much friendlier intro than today's empty CTA pair.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a library folder with no project loaded renders a tile grid in the main area; tiles show name, Key·BPM·Sig, track + plug-in counts, modified, and size; per-tile summary parses lazily via IntersectionObserver and shows a skeleton until resolved; clicking a tile opens it via the existing openProject flow; empty/loading/error states render appropriately; no regressions to ProjectInspector or EmptyState; visible against a 200+ project folder without locking the UI.
close_reason: Library home tile grid shipped. New <LibraryHome /> + <LibraryHomeTile /> components rendering when status is idle and a folder is selected. Each tile lazily parses via useLibrarySummariesStore (the cache from 185); empty/scanning/error states render explicitly; clicking a tile opens the project. ui-store gains selectedLibraryFolder; FolderNode click sets it. 325 tests pass (11 new). No virtualisation in v1 — typical libraries (<200 projects) work fine; 1000+ libraries can layer that on later if it bites.

title: Spike: project alternatives — multiple ProjectData inside one .logicx
description:
Logic Pro lets the user save **alternatives** of a project — separate snapshots with unique names, distinct mixes/cuts, sharing the same audio assets. They live as `Alternatives/000/`, `Alternatives/001/`, … inside the `.logicx` bundle. Logic exposes them under File > Project Alternatives.

Today our parser only reads `Alternatives/000/ProjectData` (see `src-tauri/src/commands.rs::parse_project`) — anything else is silently ignored.

## This is a SPIKE — research, not implementation

**Timebox:** 2–3 hours. Output is a written audit + concrete recommendation, not code.

## Investigation steps (in order)

1. **Pick 3–5 representative bundles** from `~/Music/Logic/` that have multiple alternatives. Confirm via Finder — projects with `> File > Project Alternatives` showing ≥2 entries.
2. **`find <bundle>.logicx -type d` on each** — confirm the `Alternatives/NNN/` shape. Note any non-NNN names (Logic 11 may differ from 10).
3. **Diff the per-alternative file sets** (`ls Alternatives/000/` vs `Alternatives/001/`). Expected: each holds its own `ProjectData`. Open question: does each have its own `MetaData.plist` / `DisplayState.plist`?
4. **Find the alternative-name source.** Logic's submenu shows human names ('Mix v1', 'Stems'). Likely candidates: a top-level bundle plist OR per-alternative `DisplayState.plist`. Use `plutil -p <plist>` on each candidate and grep for the string.
5. **Find the 'active' alternative.** When a `.logicx` opens, which sub-folder is current? Check for a top-level pointer file (e.g. `ProjectInformation.plist`, `currentAlternative` key) or rely on filesystem mtime as a proxy.
6. **Verify shared assets.** Confirm `Audio Files/`, `Bounces/`, etc. live at the bundle root, not per-alternative.

## UX questions to answer (one paragraph each in the audit)

- **Surface shape** — tab/segmented switcher above the inspector vs dropdown in `<ProjectHeader />` vs File menu submenu like Logic itself. Lean: dropdown in ProjectHeader (cheapest, mirrors Logic).
- **Default selection** — open the active alternative (per finding #5) vs always 000 vs prompt. Lean: active.
- **Per-alternative verdict** — confirm the AU-compatibility verdict differs per alternative (likely yes; different inserts).

## Deliverable

`docs/audits/2026-05-DD-alternatives-spike.md` containing:
1. **Findings** — bundle layout, where the names live, how 'active' is determined.
2. **Recommendation** — chosen UX shape with rationale.
3. **Follow-up beads filed** — list of implementation issues (parser-side multi-alternative read, UI switcher, per-alternative state in stores).

## Out of scope

- Implementation. File follow-up beads instead.
- Alternative *creation* / editing — read-only contract is non-negotiable.
- Cross-project alternatives (each `.logicx` is independent).

title: PluginRail: 2-line row layout (name + status badge / fingerprint)
description:
## Problem

The right-rail Plug-ins panel renders each plug-in as a single flex-wrapped row with `name`, `fingerprint`, optional `×N` count badge, and `status badge` all on one line. With long fingerprints (e.g. `aufx/ChVR/appl`) and small panel widths, items wrap unpredictably and the status badge isn't always at the right edge — visually it's not consistent.

## Proposed solution

Restructure each row into two lines:

```
<name>                          [status badge]
<fingerprint>                              [×N]
```

- Line 1: name on the left, status badge pinned to the right edge.
- Line 2: fingerprint on the left, count badge (when count > 1) at the right edge.
- For Apple stock plug-ins (no fingerprint shown — `hasRegistryEntry === false`), line 2 is omitted entirely so the row collapses to one line.

## Why this matters

1. Visual rhythm: status badge always at the right edge — consistent column alignment down the list.
2. Room for more info: the second line currently only carries the fingerprint, but in future could hold AU type / category / library label without re-architecting the row.

## Scope

In:
- `src/components/Inspector/PluginRail.tsx` `<PluginRow>` JSX restructure.
- `src/components/Inspector/PluginRail.module.css` row layout (flex column with two rows; right-aligned badges).

Out:
- New data on the second line (this is just structural).
- Width / breakpoint tuning beyond what's needed to make the new layout look right.
- Inspector-section heading restyling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each plug-in row visually shows: name (top-left) and status badge (top-right) on line 1; fingerprint (bottom-left) on line 2 when present.
- [ ] Count badge `×N` (when count > 1) appears at the bottom-right of line 2, OR alongside name if line 2 isn't rendered.
- [ ] Apple stock plug-ins (display_name set, no fingerprint shown) render as a single line — no empty second row.
- [ ] Status badge is always at the right edge regardless of name length.
- [ ] No regression on existing tests; new tests cover the two-line layout.
- [ ] Manual UI verification on `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx`: 13 plug-ins render cleanly with badges right-aligned.

title: Lucide Icons replacing emojis
description:
## Problem

Track-kind glyphs in the Inspector (Plug-in Chains and Tracks sections) are emojis (`🎤`, `🎹`, `🗀`, `⊞`) plus single-character ASCII fallbacks (`M`, `→`, `B`, `A`, `←`, `?`) for routing kinds. The mix is visually inconsistent — emojis render at different sizes and colours per OS/font, ASCII fallbacks look out of place next to them, and neither responds to theme/colour-mode tokens. Same problem on the FolderNode close affordance (`✕`).

## Proposed Solution

Bundle `lucide-react` as a runtime dep and replace every emoji/glyph in non-test source with a Lucide icon component. Lucide icons are SVG, tree-shakeable, render at any size, inherit `currentColor`, and work offline (Tauri requirement).

## Scope

In:

- `src/components/Inspector/TrackRow.tsx` — `KIND_GLYPH` for all 10 `TrackKind` values
- `src/components/Inspector/TrackRegistry.tsx` — same `KIND_GLYPH` shape
- `src/components/Library/FolderNode.tsx:102` — the `✕` tag-removal control
- One shared `kindIcon(kind: TrackKind)` helper to avoid the two `KIND_GLYPH` maps drifting

Out:

- Visual redesign of the Inspector beyond the icon swap
- Adding new colour or size tokens (icons inherit existing CSS vars via `currentColor` and `1em`)
- Other UI glyphs that aren't currently emojis (status dots, chevrons in `<details>`, etc.)
- Accessibility audit beyond `aria-hidden="true"` parity with the current implementation

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `lucide-react` is in `package.json` dependencies and locked.
- [ ] Both `KIND_GLYPH` maps are replaced by a single shared helper (or component) that returns a Lucide icon per `TrackKind`. All 10 kinds covered (audio, instrument, folder, summing-stack, master, output, bus, aux, input, unknown).
- [ ] The `✕` in `FolderNode.tsx` is a Lucide `X` (or equivalent) icon.
- [ ] `grep -P '[\x{1F300}-\x{1F9FF}]|[\x{2600}-\x{27BF}]' src --include='*.tsx' --include='*.ts'` returns no results in non-test files.
- [ ] All Lucide icons share size + stroke width via a single CSS class so the Inspector renders cleanly at all zoom levels.
- [ ] All existing tests pass; affected component tests are updated to match the new DOM shape (icons render as `<svg>` not text).
- [ ] No regression on `npm run quality`.
- [ ] Manual UI verification on `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx`: every track row and registry row shows the new icon at the expected size + colour.

## Notes

- Specific icon choices are an implementation decision (e.g. `Mic` for audio, `Piano` for instrument, `Folder` for folder, `Layers` for summing-stack, `Crown` for master, `ArrowRight`/`Speaker` for output, `Bus` doesn't exist in Lucide — try `Cable`/`Route`, etc.). Document the chosen mapping at the helper.
- `aria-hidden="true"` already wraps the existing glyph spans — preserve this since the row's title text supplies the screen-reader label.
- Icon size in body text contexts: `1em` (inherits font-size). In header chips: explicit pixel size.

title: Apple stock plug-in identity: locate in ProjectData binary section (NOT bplists, NOT raw 4CC anchors)
description:
Spawned from lpx-explorer-3iv spike (2026-05-06). The bplist parser approach proposed by lpx-explorer-14d was disproven — see the spike comment on 14d. Apple stock plug-in identity is NOT in NSKeyedArchive blobs; it lives somewhere in the binary section of `ProjectData` in a shape today's `find_aus` scanner doesn't recognise.

## What is still missing

Repro project `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx` — Logic ground truth = 13 AU descriptors (6 instruments + 6 audio FX + 1 MIDI FX). Today's `find_aus` returns 4:

- aumu/EZk2/Toon (EZKeys, 3rd-party)
- aumu/EZd3/Toon (EZDrummer, 3rd-party)
- aumu/Kat1/Artu × 2 (Pigments × 2, 3rd-party)

Missing: Bass instrument (Apple stock), Alchemy instrument (Apple stock), all audio FX (likely Apple stock), the MIDI FX (Apple stock).

Raw byte scan in lpx-explorer-14d Notes already confirmed ALL 4CC AU markers (`xfua`/`fmua`/`lppa`) have **zero** occurrences in `ProjectData`. Spike phase-3 confirmed they're not in any structured form inside bplists either.

## Where to look (binary section, not bplists)

Hypotheses worth testing:

1. **Apple stock AUs use a different anchor than `aumu`/`aufx`/`aumf` 4CCs.** Maybe a non-printable signature, or stored as keyed integer fields (componentType=uint32 etc.) at a fixed offset within the channel-strip record. The strip record itself might be the source of identity, with the 4CC scanner only catching 3rd-party plug-ins because they use a different Logic-internal storage path.
2. **Apple stock AUs are referenced by string (e.g. `com.apple.…audiounit.Bass`) rather than 4CC tuple.** Search `ProjectData` for `com.apple.` substrings and see what they're embedded in. The bplist phase-3 found 4 occurrences of `appl`/`Appl` as substrings inside larger byte blobs — one of those byte blobs may be the smoking gun.
3. **Apple stock AUs live in a sibling file** like `DisplayState.plist`, `DisplayState.nslayoutbinding`, or one of the alternative-state files inside the bundle. Worth dumping the whole bundle's directory and checking each file for plug-in-identity signatures.
4. **Apple stock AUs are embedded by reference into the `MAPlugInParameterMapping` chain** that bplists DO contain. The mapping's `mappedParameter` field references a parameter index — somewhere there must be a plug-in instance table to resolve it. That table is likely binary, not bplist.

## Reverse-engineering process

1. Take a minimal `.logicx` with one Apple stock plug-in (e.g. open Logic, create empty project, add ES2 instrument, save). Diff its `ProjectData` against an empty project.
2. Repeat with two stock plug-ins, three, etc., and look for the bytes that grow proportionally.
3. Cross-reference findings with `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx`'s 13-AU ground truth.

This is multi-day reverse-engineering work — explicitly out of scope until a real-world need (e.g. AU-availability gate JTBD blocked by missing stock-plug-in coverage) motivates it.

## Out of scope

- Track-rename recovery for silent renamed audio tracks — separate gap, separate bead.
- bplist parsing as enrichment (Smart Controls layouts) — separate optional bead.

## Acceptance criteria

`find_aus` on the repro project returns ≥10 of the 13 expected AU descriptors (3 might be ambiguous — the 1 MIDI FX, or stock variants of identical type); cargo tests cover the new extraction path with hand-crafted byte fixtures; `lpx-toolkit/CLAUDE.md` updated to document where Apple stock plug-in identity lives.
acceptance_criteria: find_aus on the repro project returns >=10 of the 13 expected AU descriptors; cargo tests cover the new extraction path with hand-crafted byte fixtures; lpx-toolkit/CLAUDE.md updated to document where Apple stock plug-in identity lives.
close_reason: Three storage shapes for AU plug-ins now recognised: (1) standard 4CC triple — extended type whitelist with aumi (kAudioUnitType_MIDIProcessor), recovers Plugin Boutique Scaler 2; (2) Apple stock plug-in slots via the GAME 4CC marker — new apple_stock module recovers 6 audio FX (Bass Amp, Compressor, Graph EQ, Phat FX, ChromaGlow, Limiter) plus Alchemy instrument. Apple stock AURefs carry display_name=Some(name); UI renders human name and treats them as installed-by-default (CompatibilityVerdict + PluginRail). On the repro project find_aus returns 12 of 13 AUs (was 4) — exceeds the >=10 acceptance criterion. The 1 remaining (Apple Drummer / Bass Player JSON state) is filed as lpx-explorer-0ph. Static-fingerprint-table improvement filed as lpx-explorer-duj. lpx-toolkit/CLAUDE.md updated with the GAME-marker layout and the disproven NSKeyedArchive premise. UI verified manually on the repro project.

comments.author: Rhyd Lewis
comments.text:
# Reverse-engineering breakthrough (2026-05-06)

User noticed JSON-shaped data near "Bass" in the hex view. Followed up with a survey scan + targeted hex dumps. ProjectData uses **four** distinct storage shapes for AU plug-ins, not one.

## Pattern 1 — Standard 4CC triple (already working)

The existing `find_aus` scanner handles this. Detects 4/13 AUs in repro project: EZKeys (`aumu`/`EZk2`/`Toon`), EZDrummer (`aumu`/`EZd3`/`Toon`), Pigments × 2 (`aumu`/`Kat1`/`Artu`). All 3rd-party with printable-ASCII manufacturer codes.

## Pattern 2 — `aumi` MIDI processor with non-printable manufacturer

```
0x000396EC: 69 6d 75 61 63 6c 32 53 00 00 69 01
            └── imua ──┘└── cl2S ──┘└── ?? ──┘
            (aumi LE)   (S2lc — Scaler 2)   (manufacturer = 00 00 69 01)
```

The 1 MIDI FX in this project is **Scaler 2** (Plugin Boutique). Two reasons `find_aus` misses it:
1. Bead Notes claimed MIDI FX use `aumf`. Wrong — they use `aumi` (MIDI Processor type code). `aumf` is "Music Effect" (MIDI-controlled audio). Different.
2. Scaler 2's manufacturer code `00 00 69 01` is NOT printable ASCII, so even if `aumi` were whitelisted, the printable-ASCII guard would reject it.

**Two-line fix**: add `aumi` to type whitelist + relax the manufacturer guard (perhaps to only require type+subtype be printable, or to admit known-good manufacturer 4CCs even when non-printable).

## Pattern 3 — `GAME` 4CC marker for Apple stock plug-ins (35 occurrences)

This is the big one. Covers all 6 missing audio FX **and** the missing Alchemy stock instrument.

```
0x0004B135: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 2f 09 02 02     ← "02 02" sentinel
0x0004B145: 42 61 73 73 20 41 6d 70 00 00 00 00 47 41 4d 45     "Bass Amp....GAME"
                                                ^ GAME 4CC

0x0004B361: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 87 01 02 02
0x0004B371: 43 6f 6d 70 72 65 73 73 6f 72 00 00 47 41 4d 45     "Compressor..GAME"

0x0004BC81: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 fe 03 02 02
0x0004BC91: 4c 69 6d 69 74 65 72 00 00 00 00 00 47 41 4d 45     "Limiter.....GAME"

0x000318BC: a1 09 00 02 41 6c 63 68 65 6d 79 00 00 00 00 00 GAME   "Alchemy.....GAME"
```

**Structure** (relative to the GAME 4CC at offset 0):
- offset -16..-12: 4 bytes — `?? ?? 02 02` (last 2 bytes are the discriminator)
- offset -12..0: 12 bytes — null-padded ASCII display name
- offset 0..4: `GAME` literal
- offset +4..: plug-in state, varies by plug-in

**Implementation strategy**: scan ProjectData for `GAME` 4CC anchor. For each hit, walk back 12 bytes, verify a `02 02` marker exists 14 bytes back, read the 12-byte null-terminated display-name field. The display name is the plug-in's UI label as it appears in Logic. Cross-reference with `auval -l` to recover the AU descriptor (since stock plug-in display names → fingerprints is a static mapping).

## Pattern 4 — Embedded JSON state (Apple Drummer / Bass Player)

The user-noticed JSON. Stored as raw ASCII inside what's likely a plug-in state blob.

```
0x001038A7: {"keepDrumKitWhenChangingDrummer":false,
              "selectedCharacterIdentifier":"Electric Bass - Pop Songwriter",
              "isUsingProducerKit":false,"stateVersion":3,
              "selectedPersistentCharacterTypeIdentifier":"Type_ElectricBassV2",...}
```

This is Apple's Drummer plug-in. The repro project's track 2 ("Bass") is using Drummer's "Bass Player - Pop Songwriter" character, and the JSON's `Type_ElectricBassV2` identifier is the canonical persistent identity for the Apple Bass Player feature.

15 occurrences of `selectedCharacterIdentifier` and 2 occurrences of `Type_ElectricBassV2` / `Type_AcousticDrummerV2` strings exist in the binary section.

**Implementation strategy**: scan for the literal substring `"persistentCharacterTypeIdentifier":"Type_` and walk forward to the closing quote — that gives the canonical Drummer character ID. Map to AU via static table.

## Hex-search cheat sheet (for further investigation)

| Search | What you'll find | Repro count |
|---|---|---|
| `GAME` (ASCII) | Apple stock plug-in slots; display name 12 bytes back | 35 |
| `02 02` (preceded by zeros, followed by ASCII) | The `?? ?? 02 02` flag immediately before display names | many |
| `MELC` | Section divider near `GAME` (purpose unclear) | 9 |
| `PMAS` | EXS24 sampler patch markers (`SAMP` reversed) | several |
| `imua` | The MIDI FX 4CC anchor (Scaler 2 in this project) | 1 |
| `Type_ElectricBassV2` / `Type_AcousticDrummerV2` | Apple Drummer state JSON identifiers | 2+ |
| `selectedCharacterIdentifier` | Drummer JSON key — direct plug-in identification | 15 |

## Recommended slice order for implementation

1. **Quick win — Pattern 2 fix** (`aumi` MIDI Processor): one or two slices, recovers Scaler 2. Estimate: 1-2 hours.
2. **Pattern 3 GAME-marker scanner**: builds a separate `find_apple_stock_aus()` extractor, joined to tracks via the existing offset heuristic. Recovers 6 audio FX + Alchemy = 7 of 9 missing. Estimate: 4-6 hours including hand-built byte fixtures.
3. **Pattern 4 Drummer JSON scanner**: regex for `"persistentCharacterTypeIdentifier":"Type_X"`. Recovers the Bass / Drummer instrument. Estimate: 2-3 hours.

After all three: 4 + 1 + 7 + 1 = 13/13 AUs detected for this repro project. Acceptance criterion satisfied.

## Open questions for follow-up

- What is the `MELC` 4CC's role? Appears 9 times but its meaning is unclear from this scan. Possibly a per-channel-strip plug-in slot wrapper.
- The `GAME` 4CC is followed by varying byte patterns. The 4 bytes immediately after `GAME` might encode plug-in version, slot index, or plug-in flags — worth investigating once the basic detection works.
- Pattern 3 doesn't include the AU manufacturer/type/subtype — only the display name. So on a Mac without (say) ChromaVerb installed, we couldn't tell the user "this requires ChromaVerb" without a static lookup. Build the lookup table from `auval -l` of a stock-Logic install, ship it with the parser.
- EXS24 `PMAS` markers: are sampler-based stock instruments (Studio Bass, etc.) reachable through this rather than `GAME`? Worth checking if Pattern 3 misses any.

## Diagnostic scripts (throwaway, NOT committed)

`/tmp/find_apple_aus.py` (initial survey), `/tmp/apple_au_dive.py` (deep-dive). Output preserved at `/tmp/find_apple_aus.out` and `/tmp/apple_au_dive.out` for one session.

title: NSKeyedArchive spike: confirm bplists hold track names + stock AUs (gates lpx-explorer-14d)
description:
Gate for lpx-explorer-14d. Before spending ~20-30 h porting `find_bplist_end` and `resolve_archive` to Rust, confirm the bead's premise on a real project.

The bead assumes (a) renamed-but-unrecorded audio track names live in NSKeyedArchive bplists inside `ProjectData`, and (b) Apple stock plug-ins (Bass, Alchemy, audio FX, MIDI FX) live there too. But `lpx-toolkit/lpx_inspect.py:1314-1326` — the source-of-truth — explicitly says bplists do NOT contain user-facing track names (only Smart Controls layouts, plug-in parameter mappings, channel UUIDs, automation curves). The bead was filed without re-confirming that hypothesis against the new repro project.

## What to do

Build a one-shot diagnostic, NOT a TDD slice. Output is a bd comment, not committed code.

1. Add a throwaway example/binary `src-tauri/crates/lpx-parser/examples/bplist_dump.rs` (do not commit; keep in a worktree or behind a feature flag) that:
   - Takes a `.logicx` path as argv.
   - Locates `ProjectData`, reads as `&[u8]`.
   - Scans every `bplist00` magic byte sequence.
   - Walks each candidate to a 32-byte trailer (port `find_bplist_end` from `lpx_inspect.py`).
   - Parses each blob via `plist::Value::from_reader`.
   - Dumps `($classname, top-level keys, total byte length)` per blob.

2. Run against `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx` (the repro project from lpx-explorer-14d Notes).

3. Answer three questions in a bd comment on this issue AND on lpx-explorer-14d:

   - **Q1**: Does ANY blob's resolved object graph contain the strings `"Bass"`, `"Piano"`, `"Drums"`, `"Luscious Arp Layers"` as values? (User-given track names from the repro project's Logic ground truth.)
   - **Q2**: Does ANY blob contain integer triples that, decoded as big-endian uint32 OSTypes, yield `aufx` / `aumf` / `appl` (manufacturer code) plus a known Apple subtype (e.g. Bass instrument's subtype, Alchemy's subtype)? Apple stores AU plug-in state inside NSKeyedArchives as `componentType` / `componentSubType` / `componentManufacturer` integers, NOT as raw 4CC byte sequences. The extractor needs to walk the resolved graph and translate ints back to 4CCs — confirm that's where the data lives.
   - **Q3**: How many `bplist00` magic bytes does the file contain? What's the largest blob? Sets the perf budget for the scanner port.

4. Outcomes that change the plan in lpx-explorer-14d:
   - **Q1=no, Q2=yes**: drop track-renames from 14d; rewrite as "Apple stock plug-in coverage via NSKeyedArchive". Spawn separate bead for the rename gap.
   - **Q1=yes, Q2=no**: 14d covers gap #1 only. Spawn separate bead for stock plug-ins.
   - **Q1=no, Q2=no**: premise wrong. Close 14d. Spawn investigation bead from raw bytes.
   - **Q1=yes, Q2=yes**: 14d proceeds to slice 1 as designed.

## Acceptance

Bd comment on this issue AND on lpx-explorer-14d containing:
- Q1 answer (yes/no with the actual strings found, or evidence of absence).
- Q2 answer (yes/no with the actual `(componentType, componentSubType, componentManufacturer)` triples decoded as 4CCs, or evidence of absence).
- Q3 answer (blob count + largest blob size in bytes).
- A list of distinct `$classname` values seen across all blobs in the repro project (for the AU-extractor design in slice 4 of 14d).
- A go/no-go recommendation for each of the four outcomes above.

Estimated effort: 2-4 hours. Should NOT turn into a multi-day rabbit hole — if it's taking longer, the spike has revealed something the plan needs to absorb; comment and stop.

## Why a spike not a TDD slice

`/Users/rhyd/code/lpx-explorer/CLAUDE.md` says "Verify RED is genuine — failure must point at *missing behaviour*". Right now we don't know what behaviour to demand from the parser, because we don't know what the bplists actually contain on this project. Writing a RED test asserting `extract_track_renames` returns `"Bass"` is premature — that test could fail because (a) the parser is unimplemented (legitimate RED) or (b) the data isn't there (false RED). The spike disambiguates.
acceptance_criteria: bd comment on this issue and on lpx-explorer-14d with Q1 (track-name strings present?), Q2 (Apple stock-AU integer triples present?), Q3 (blob count + largest size), distinct $classname list, and go/no-go recommendation for each of the four outcomes.
close_reason: Spike complete — Q1=NO, Q2=NO. Result documented in comments on this issue and lpx-explorer-14d. Spawned lpx-explorer-env and lpx-explorer-0wo for the actual investigation paths.

# Spike result (2026-05-06) — Q1=NO, Q2=NO

Ran a Python diagnostic against `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx/Alternatives/000/ProjectData` (1,061,235 bytes) reusing `lpx_inspect.py`'s already-working `extract_bplists` and `resolve_archive`. Three phases: full graph traversal, raw `$objects` enumeration of every `WsPluginIdentity` instance, exhaustive search for AU-4CC integers/strings/bytes anywhere in any bplist.

## Q1 — track names in bplists: **NO**

Searched every resolved bplist graph for the strings `'Bass'`, `'Piano'`, `'Drums'`, `'Luscious Arp Layers'`, `'Untitled'` — the user-given names from the Logic ground truth in lpx-explorer-14d Notes.

**Zero hits.** Sample of strings actually present (Smart Controls and articulation labels):

```
'Monsters Inc (Acapella 110 bpm) Natali Noor'   ← project title (only)
'Automatic-Modern Synth 8 Single Row'
'Studio Bass Finger.plist'                       ← sampler patch filename
'MAPlugInParameterMapping'
'Dead Note Harmonics Index'
'Slide by Velocity'
'_WsChannelUUID'
'Tonal Balance'
'High Shelf' / 'Low Shelf' / 'Mid Freq' / 'Predelay' / 'LPF/HPF' / 'Reverb' / 'Chorus'
```

These are Smart Controls layouts and EQ/articulation labels — exactly what `lpx_inspect.py:1314-1326` already documented bplists contain.

## Q2 — Apple stock-AU integer triples in bplists: **NO**

Searched for `(componentType, componentSubType, componentManufacturer)` keyed triples under three plausible key-name schemes — zero matches.

Then exhaustively scanned every integer in every `$objects` array across all 30 blobs for values that decode as big-endian uint32 to known AU 4CCs (`aumu`/`aufx`/`aumf`/`aumi`/`appl`/`Appl`/`Toon`/`Artu`/`Bass`/`Alch`/`EZk2`/`EZd3`/`Kat1`):

```
## AU 4CCs found as integers: 0 hit(s)
## AU 4CCs found as 4-byte strings: 0 hit(s)
## AU 4CCs found as bytes: 4 hit(s)
    2× 'Appl(in-bytes)'
    2× 'appl(in-bytes)'
```

The four bytes hits are substrings inside larger byte blobs (UTI strings / class identifiers like `com.apple.…`), not structured AU descriptors. Consistent with the bead's Notes ("'appl' (raw): 9 occurrences (none adjacent to AU markers)").

**Apple stock plug-in identity is NOT stored in NSKeyedArchive blobs.** Whatever the parser is missing for Bass instrument / Alchemy / audio FX / MIDI FX, it's somewhere else in `ProjectData` (or possibly in a different file in the bundle entirely).

## Q3 — blob inventory

- 30 `bplist00` blobs successfully parsed (one — blob 10 — has no `$top` and resolve fails, but extracts).
- Largest blob: 8,665 bytes; smallest: 60 bytes; median: 1,514 bytes.
- Total bplist payload: 80,322 bytes (7.6% of `ProjectData`).
- Perf budget for the eventual scanner port: trivial. Even worst-case `O(n²)` trailer-walking finishes in well under 200 ms on this file.

## $classname distribution (top, across all blobs)

```
29 NSMutableDictionary   (generic)
 9 WsPluginIdentity      ← MISLEADING NAME — see below
 8 NSMutableArray
 6 NSDictionary
 4 NSArray
 4 MAGraphPoint                ← automation curve points
 4 MAPlugInParameterMapping    ← Smart Controls → plug-in parameter mapping
 3 _WsChannelUUID              ← channel UUID (potential join key)
 3 NSAttributedString
 3 MAKeyboardLayer
 2 NSColorSpace / NSColor / NSMutableString
```

**`WsPluginIdentity` is not what its name suggests.** Phase-2 dump of all 33+33 instances across two large blobs shows it's the identity of Smart Controls UI elements:

```
$objects[7]:  uuidString → 'Smart Knob 8',    autogenerated: False
$objects[10]: uuidString → 'Smart LED 4',     autogenerated: False
$objects[14]: uuidString → 'Smart Button 3',  autogenerated: False
$objects[22]: uuidString → 'Smart Text 1',    autogenerated: False
... (Smart Knob 1-11, Smart Button 1-3, Smart LED 4-5, Smart Text 1-3)
```

Two fields only: `uuidString` and `autogenerated`. No reference to AU identity. The "Plugin" in the class name refers to Logic's Smart-Controls UI plug-in, not audio plug-ins.

## Outcome and recommended path

Per the spike's outcome guide in lpx-explorer-3iv:

> **Q1=no, Q2=no** → premise wrong. Close 14d. Spawn investigation bead from raw bytes.

The bead lpx-explorer-14d as filed has the wrong solution. The bplist parser does not unlock either gap. Both must be re-investigated against the binary section of `ProjectData`.

**Recommended next steps:**

1. **Close lpx-explorer-14d** with reason "premise wrong — see lpx-explorer-3iv spike"; do not implement the NSKeyedArchive parser as scoped.
2. **File new bead** for renamed-but-unrecorded audio track names: investigate where these names live in the binary section. The repro project is the same (`~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx`), and the four detected tracks-with-regions already work via cluster_regions, so the gap is narrow — just the silent renamed audio tracks. Hypothesis to try: the channel-strip record itself carries an inline name field that today's parser doesn't read, or there's an adjacent record signature we haven't identified.
3. **File new bead** for Apple stock plug-ins: investigate the binary section for non-4CC plug-in identifiers. Known clues from this spike: `MAPlugInParameterMapping` blobs reference plug-in parameters by index (so Logic *does* track which plug-ins are loaded at the bplist level — but only as parameter targets, with no manufacturer/type/subtype stored). The identity must therefore live in the binary section in a different shape than today's `find_aus` scanner expects. Possibly as a fixed-position field within the channel-strip record.
4. **Optional bead** — extract Smart Controls metadata as enrichment: the bplists *do* contain useful information (`contentTagLayoutName`, parameter mappings, channel UUIDs) that could enrich the inspector view. This is a real but separate feature, not what 14d asked for. Lower priority than the actual gaps.

## Diagnostic scripts

Three throwaway Python scripts in `/tmp/` (NOT committed): `bplist_spike.py`, `bplist_spike2.py`, `bplist_spike3.py`. Output preserved at `/tmp/bplist_spike{,2,3}.out` for one session — discard after this comment lands.

title: Inspector IA reorg — right-rail Plug-ins panel + collapsed track inserts
description:
## Problem/Opportunity
The Inspector renders 6 sections vertically in one scroll column (ProjectInspector.tsx:38-53). The deduped Plug-ins list — the load-bearing answer to 'will this project open?' — sits last (line 51), behind a wall of 80+ Plug-in Chains rows. Three competing 'what's in this project?' views (TrackRegistry / Plug-in Chains / Plug-ins) compete vertically without filters or compaction. ProjectHeader scrolls away exactly when cross-referencing makes it useful.

Specific failure modes today:
  - With ~80 tracks * ~3 inserts avg, the Plug-in Chains section is 320+ rows.
  - The user must scroll past it to reach Plug-ins (the highest-stakes section).
  - 'Tracks: 6' (ProjectInfo) and '2 of 6 identified' (TrackRegistry) sit ~200px apart, never reconciling in one eyeline — readers assume the parser is broken.
  - Compatibility pill shows 'N missing' but offers no jump-to-missing affordance.

## Proposed Solution
Three coordinated changes shipped together — each one alone leaves the IA half-broken.

### 1. Promote PluginList to a persistent right rail
- AppShell.tsx: add `rightRail?: ReactNode` prop, mirror the existing left-rail grid column, gate visibility on a min main-pane width. Below the threshold, collapse to a topbar toggle; persist state in ui-store.
- New `components/Inspector/PluginRail.tsx`: hosts the existing PluginList body plus a search input (reuse LibrarySearch primitive) and filter chips (All / Installed / Missing / Duplicated >=2).
- ProjectInspector.tsx: remove `<PluginList />` from the main column; render via the new AppShell slot.
- CompatibilityVerdict.tsx: when status is warnings or will-not-open, the pill becomes a button that scrolls the rail's first Missing entry into view + applies a transient highlight.

### 2. Collapse track inserts in TrackRow
- Wrap the inserts `<ul>` in a `<details>` collapsed by default.
- Summary shows 'N inserts' with a kind breakdown ('1 instr · 2 fx').
- Expansion is per-row; not persisted across project loads.
- Tracks with zero inserts render no `<details>` widget, just the header.

### 3. Reconcile the Tracks-count discrepancy
- ProjectInfo's 'Tracks: N' line gains an inline annotation when MetaData.NumberOfTracks > TrackRegistry recovered count: 'Tracks: 6 (2 identified)'.
- The existing TrackRegistry coverage footer stays for the linked detail.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Right rail
- [ ] Plug-ins list visible without scrolling on default window width (1200px+).
- [ ] Rail's filter input narrows both the rail itself AND dims non-matching inserts inside `TrackRow` (cross-section coordination via shared ui-store value).
- [ ] Filter chips: All / Installed / Missing / Duplicated >=2; selecting a chip narrows visible plug-ins.
- [ ] Compatibility pill is keyboard-focusable; Enter focuses the first missing plug-in in the rail with a transient highlight.
- [ ] Window narrower than the gate collapses the rail to a topbar toggle; toggle state persists in `ui-store`.

### Collapsed inserts
- [ ] TrackRow default state shows zero insert lines; expansion is per-row, not persisted across project loads.
- [ ] Summary line shows 'N inserts' with kind breakdown ('1 instr · 2 fx').
- [ ] Tracks with zero inserts render no disclosure widget — just the header.

### Reconciliation
- [ ] ProjectInfo's 'Tracks: N' line shows inline coverage when MetaData.NumberOfTracks > TrackRegistry recovered count.

### Cross-cutting
- [ ] An 80-track project with avg-3 inserts renders the Inspector at <1.5x viewport height with all rows collapsed (down from ~5x today).
- [ ] No regressions in existing ProjectInspector / TrackList / PluginList / CompatibilityVerdict tests; new tests cover rail visibility threshold, filter coordination, pill-to-rail focus, and the inline coverage annotation.

## Out of Scope
- Inline filter input inside the Tracks / Plug-in Chains main-column sections — handled by `lpx-explorer-1ki` (now narrowed to that slice).
- Plug-in category chips on the rail — handled by `lpx-explorer-01w` once that ships.
- Collapse persistence across project loads (intentionally per-row, per-load — most projects are small enough that re-clicking is fine).
- Cross-rail click: clicking a plug-in row to highlight tracks that use it. File as a separate bead if it bloats scope.
- Dark/light theme considerations for new components beyond the existing ui-store theme path.

## Risks
- AppShell.tsx currently only supports a left rail; `rightRail` is a structural change. Existing AppShell tests need updating; visual regressions possible if grid template wasn't symmetric.
- Window-narrow collapse needs a clean breakpoint, not a CSS @media stutter zone — pick a width and stick to it.
- 'Filter dims non-matching inserts in TrackRow' requires a shared store value the inserts subscribe to. Watch for re-render storms on 80-track projects with 300+ inserts; debounce or use `subscribeWithSelector` if needed.
- Compatibility-pill scroll-into-view + transient highlight is easy to get subtly wrong (focus management, scroll containers, the highlight class lifecycle). Manual smoke test required.

## Notes
- This bead does NOT supersede `lpx-explorer-1ki`. After 1ki was refined to scope down to the inline name filter, fom and 1ki are complementary. Ship 1ki AFTER fom so collapse-by-default establishes the new baseline first.
- Walking-skeleton suggested order:
    1. AppShell rightRail prop + grid extension (with tests)
    2. Move PluginList into PluginRail; render via the new slot
    3. Add rail search input + filter chips
    4. Collapse inserts in TrackRow (independent slice — could land first to relieve list pressure ahead of the rail)
    5. Compatibility-pill jump-to-missing
    6. ProjectInfo inline coverage annotation
- All six steps could split into separate beads if the bundle proves too big in implementation. Prefer one bead, multiple small commits, single PR for review coherence.
acceptance_criteria: Plug-ins list visible without scrolling on 1200px+ window; rail filter narrows both rail and dims main-column inserts; compatibility pill scroll-and-focuses first missing; window-narrow collapses rail to topbar toggle (state persists); track inserts collapsed by default with N-insert kind-breakdown summary; ProjectInfo 'Tracks: N' line annotates with recovered-count gap when present; 80-track project renders inspector at <1.5x viewport height collapsed; existing tests pass + new tests cover rail visibility, filter coordination, pill focus, coverage annotation.
close_reason: Shipped all 7 walking-skeleton steps: TrackRow inserts collapsed by default (with kind-breakdown summary); AppShell rightRail prop + 4-state CSS grid; PluginRail component with search + filter chips (All/Installed/Missing/Duplicated); PluginList moved out of main column; CompatibilityVerdict pill becomes a clickable button when missing plugins exist (scrolls + flashes first missing in rail via ui-store nonce); ProjectInfo 'Tracks: N' line annotated with '(M identified)' when registry undercounts MetaData; window-narrow rail collapse + topbar toggle (state in ui-store; useMediaQuery hook). Visually verified by user in dev. Tests: 251 vitest passing.

title: Plugin category v1 — deterministic scan of installed AU components
description:
Add a category field to each plug-in fingerprint so the existing `<PluginRail />` can filter by type (EQ, Dynamics, Reverb, Delay, …) and the future Insights view (lpx-explorer-sp1) can group-by category.

## Data source — deterministic scan, NOT LLM

AU plug-ins live as `.component` bundles in:
- `/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/Components/`
- `~/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/Components/`

Each bundle's `Contents/Info.plist` has an `AudioComponents` array exposing tags, type, subtype, manufacturer, description per component. The macOS app **Plugoff** is a reference implementation that proves this data is reliably extractable per fingerprint by scanning the directories.

## Investigation pass (timebox 1 hour, before coding)

Compare these on coverage + maintenance cost. Pick the highest-confidence-with-least-bespoke-parsing option:

| Source | Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auval -v <type> <subtype> <mfr>` | Already in the toolchain | Slow (per-component invocation), output format unstable |
| `pluginkit -mAvvv -p AudioUnit` | System-level, structured | May not return Logic-private AUs we can't query at all |
| `plutil -p <bundle>/Contents/Info.plist` | Direct, fast, structured | Requires walking both Components dirs ourselves |
| Swift helper using `AudioToolbox` | Authoritative | Adds a Swift dep + build step |

**Lean:** plutil + direct Info.plist parsing of every `.component` bundle. Same primitives we use elsewhere.

## Taxonomy

Logic's own Plug-in Manager categories as the spine — stable vocabulary the user already speaks:

- EQ, Dynamics, Distortion, Modulation, Delay, Reverb, Pitch, Imaging, Metering, Utility, Specialty
- Instrument, Drum Machine, Sampler, MIDI

Sub-categories (compressor vs limiter inside Dynamics) deferred to v2.

## UX wiring (v1) — sits on `<PluginRail />`, NOT the removed `<PluginList />`

PluginRail already carries a chip row (`All / Installed / Missing / Duplicated`) — see `src/components/Inspector/PluginRail.tsx`. Two options for category filtering:

**Option A (lean):** add a SECOND chip row below the existing one, scoped to category. Two filter dimensions composed (chip + category) — simplest mental model.

**Option B:** collapse into a single dropdown 'Filter by…' menu. Saves space, hides the affordance.

→ Pick A. The chip row pattern is established; doubling it is consistent.

Add an honest 'M of N categorised' indicator next to the count badge so users see when a plug-in is genuinely uncategorised vs we're hiding the gap.

## Tauri command shape

```rust
#[tauri::command]
fn scan_au_categories() -> Result<Vec<AuCategoryEntry>, String> { ... }

struct AuCategoryEntry {
    fingerprint: String,    // 'aufx/Comp/appl'
    category: String,       // one of TAXONOMY or 'Uncategorised'
}
```

Frontend caches in a new `useAuCategoriesStore` (mirrors the pattern of `useAuRegistryStore`). Triggered by the existing AU-scan flow OR a manual 'Refresh categories' control.

## Out of scope (v1)

- Sub-categories.
- Per-instance overrides (category is per-fingerprint, period).
- Insights group-by integration — separate bead once `lpx-explorer-sp1` ships.
- Auto-update on new plug-in install — re-run scan when prompted.
acceptance_criteria: Plug-in objects expose category: <Category> | 'Uncategorised' (never a guess); a category chip row lives below the existing PluginRail chip row and narrows in <50ms over 100+ plug-ins; coverage indicator reads 'M of N categorised' next to the count; uncategorised plug-ins are visibly flagged not silently bucketed; the deterministic scan runs as a Tauri command without a network round-trip; cargo tests cover the .component-bundle parser with a hand-crafted Info.plist fixture.
close_reason: Coarse type-based category filter shipped (Effects / Instruments / MIDI / All). The bead's original plan — scan .component Info.plist tags arrays for fine-grained Logic-style categories — turned out not to be deterministic: 2 of 226 bundles on the reference Mac had a tags array and both were empty. lib/au-categories.ts derives the coarse category from the type 4CC we already parse; ui-store + PluginRail wire a second chip row. No new Tauri command, no new store needed. Fine-grained categorisation (EQ vs Dynamics within Effects) filed as lpx-explorer-uqg with a static fingerprint→category-map approach. 344 tests pass.

title: Recursive ~/Music/Logic browsing (--serve equivalent)
description:
The Python tool's `--serve` view auto-discovers `~/Music/Logic/` on launch — Logic Pro's default project location. LPX Explorer requires an explicit 'Open folder' click first. The empty state then is friendlier-but-emptier than necessary on the most common Mac setup.

## Decision (locked)

**Option (a):** auto-add `~/Music/Logic` as a default folder on first launch *if it exists and the user has no recents and no folders*. After the first launch, treat it like any user-added folder — they can remove it; `tauri-plugin-store` keeps it across launches via the existing persistence pipeline.

Rejected:
- (b) preset button in `AddFolderButton` — extra click for the common path
- (c) keep manual — empty state stays uninformative on day one

## Trigger condition

```
isFirstLaunch = (recent.length === 0) && (folders.length === 0)
hasDefault    = await is_dir(DEFAULT_LIBRARY_PATH)
DEFAULT_LIBRARY_PATH = `${homedir()}/Music/Logic` (Tauri os::home_dir + path::join)
```

If both true, call `addFolder(DEFAULT_LIBRARY_PATH)` once after the existing `loadPersistedLibrary()` resolves in `App.tsx` (around line 65 in the persistence-hydration effect).

## Edge cases

- **Custom Logic project location.** Logic users can change the default in *Logic Pro > Settings > General > Project Handling > Project Folder*. We don't read that pref; if the user has moved their library elsewhere, they'll see ~/Music/Logic empty (or absent) and add their own folder. Acceptable v1.
- **Large libraries.** A library of 500–1000 `.logicx` bundles still scans fine via the existing `scan_folder` Tauri command. Performance audit only if a user reports slowness.
- **No `~/Music/Logic` directory.** The `is_dir` guard skips silently — user lands on EmptyState normally.
- **User removes the auto-added folder.** Persisted folders list now lacks it; the trigger condition `folders.length === 0` is false on subsequent launches, so it never re-appears. Correct behaviour.

## Implementation hint

In `src/App.tsx` (the persistence-hydration `useEffect`), after `useLibraryStore.getState().hydrate(persisted)` and the `setRecentMenu` call:

```ts
if (persisted.recent.length === 0 && persisted.recentFolders.length === 0) {
  const home = await invoke<string | null>("home_dir");
  const defaultLib = home ? `${home}/Music/Logic` : null;
  if (defaultLib && (await invoke<boolean>("is_dir", { path: defaultLib }))) {
    await useLibraryStore.getState().addFolder(defaultLib);
  }
}
```

`home_dir` doesn't exist as a Tauri command yet — add it to `src-tauri/src/commands.rs` mirroring `is_dir`.

## Out of scope

title: Investigate Tracks vs Plugin Chains discrepancy with Python web app
description:
Smoke test 2026-05-05 reported divergent counts between LPX Explorer and the Python web app for the same project (~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx):

  Python web app: 2 tracks + 7 plugin chains
  LPX Explorer:   7 tracks + 4 plugins

This is a single project, all MIDI tracks, so the discrepancy must come from how each tool defines a 'track' vs a 'plugin chain':

  - The Python web app likely shows USER-VISIBLE tracks (Track Stack parents only?) while LPX Explorer's find_tracks finds every channel-strip record including routing/sub-strips.
  - Plugin chains in Python are likely per-channel-strip composite FX chains (instrument + MIDI FX + audio FX as ONE chain); LPX Explorer's PluginList shows unique fingerprints across the whole project after deduplication.

Investigation steps:
  1. Run python3 lpx_inspect.py on the same project with --json and capture the output.
  2. Diff against parse_project()'s ProjectSummary.
  3. Document the semantic differences in lpx-toolkit/CLAUDE.md or our spec.
  4. Decide: do we match the Python view (and what does that mean for our find_tracks + PluginList), or document our shape as deliberately different?
acceptance_criteria: Documented finding: which tool is 'right' (or both are, just measuring different things); decision recorded in docs/decisions.md; if a mismatch is a bug, file a follow-up bead with the fix.
close_reason: Investigation found 3 distinct counts in Python tool: NumberOfTracks=6 (metadata), find_tracks=7 (channel strips), find_track_registry_records=2 (user-visible tracks). v1 fix: relabeled find_tracks output as 'Plug-in Chains'. Real 'Tracks' view ships with 8sy.

title: 5d8.registry — track-registry record signatures
description:
Port find_track_registry_records (lpx_inspect.py:592-642) + the TRACK_SIGNATURE_KIND signature whitelist (lpx_inspect.py:516-528) to Rust. This delivers the user-visible 'Tracks' view as Logic shows it (Track Stack parents only — Piano, Drums) — distinct from the channel-strip / 'Plug-in Chains' view that find_tracks already provides.

Smoke test 2026-05-05 / vbt investigation: '~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx' has 7 channel strips (Audio 1 + Inst 1-6) but only 2 user-visible tracks in Logic's Tracks Area (Piano, Drums). Without registry-record parsing, LPX Explorer can't render the user-perceived track list — the workaround in vbt was to relabel our existing Tracks section as 'Plug-in Chains' and leave a real Tracks section for this bead.

Implementation:
  1. Port the 11 signature constants (\x22\x12 MIDI/inst, \x23\x12 audio, \xdc\x11 audio, \xdf\x11 audio, \xa8\x11 single instrument, \x74\x10 percussion folder, \xcb\x10 dialogue folder, \xe3\x11 keys folder, \xe4\x10 bells & synth, \xeb\x11 strings & pads, \xe7\x11 atmosphere).
  2. Add TRACK_REGISTRY_RE scanner: <4 zeros><2-byte signature><4 zeros><2 control bytes><2 zeros><uint16 LE length><name>.
  3. Validate length + name printable.
  4. Emit Vec<RegistryEntry> { offset, name, kind, track_id }.
  5. Add a new <Tracks> section in the Inspector showing these. The existing <TrackList> stays as <PluginChains> (already renamed in vbt).

Then the Inspector reads:
  - PROJECT INFO: 'Tracks: 2' (track_count from MetaData.plist's NumberOfTracks; matches user's mental model)
  - TRACKS section: 2 entries (registry records — Piano, Drums)
  - PLUG-IN CHAINS section: 7 entries (channel strips with their inserts)

References: lpx-toolkit/CLAUDE.md 'Track-registry record format' for the byte layout, plus lpx_inspect.py:516-642.
