title: Cross-project plug-in rollup view
description:
The Python tool's `--rollup` answers *'where do I use EZdrummer?'* across every project in the user's library. LPX Explorer's `<PluginRail />` answers it *per project* — the rollup is the same view, aggregated across all known projects.

## UX (locked)

`<PluginRail />` gains a **'This project' ⇄ 'Library'** scope toggle (segmented control or chip-style toggle in the rail header). Library scope:

- Aggregates `ProjectSummary.fingerprints[]` across `useLibraryStore.recent` + every project under `useLibraryStore.folders` whose folder has finished scanning
- Renders one row per unique fingerprint with a usage count badge (`'EZdrummer 2 — used in 14 projects'`)
- Clicking a row reveals the contributing project paths (disclosure under the row); clicking a path opens that project via the existing `openProject` flow
- The existing chip filters (All / Installed / Missing / Duplicated) and search box continue to apply, just over the rolled-up set

Considered + rejected:
- **Standalone Library view** replacing the inspector — disorienting; loses per-project context
- **Overlay / modal** — loud; doesn't fit the power-tool aesthetic

## Data strategy (locked)

Lazy parse-on-demand into a new `useLibrarySummariesStore` (in-session cache, `Map<path, ProjectSummary>`). When the user toggles to Library scope, kick off `parse_project` for every known path that's not yet cached. Rate-limited via a small worker pool (~4 concurrent) to avoid hammering the FS. Persisted summary cache across launches is a v2 concern.

## Implementation pieces (single feature, single PR)

1. `useLibrarySummariesStore` — Zustand store + tests. `getOrParse(path)` returns cached summary or invokes `parse_project` and caches.
2. `lib/library-rollup.ts` — pure function `aggregate(Map<path, ProjectSummary>) -> RolledFingerprint[]` where each entry has `fingerprint`, `count`, `projectPaths[]`. Pure; trivially testable.
3. `<PluginRail />` — scope toggle, library-scope rendering, count badge + path-disclosure UI.
4. Performance verification against ≥200 projects in the library — rate-limit parse spawns; toggle should respond <500ms cold, <50ms warm.

## Out of scope

- Persisted summary cache across launches — in-session for v1.
- Cross-project diffs ('Project A has Comp, Project B doesn't').
- Search across project NAMES from the rollup (LibraryRail's search already covers it).
- Eager pre-parse on folder-scan completion — pure optimisation; only if lazy proves too jankly under real workloads.

LABELS: ui-polish
acceptance_criteria: PluginRail gains a 'This project' / 'Library' scope toggle; Library scope shows deduped fingerprints across all known projects with usage counts; rows disclose to project names that link back via openProject; performant against 500+ projects in the library (toggle responds in <500ms cold, <50ms warm); aria-label updates to reflect scope.
close_reason: Library-scope rollup shipped. Pure lib/library-rollup.ts + Zustand library-summaries cache (lazy + de-duped) + scope toggle in PluginRail header + LibraryPluginRow with 'Used in N projects' disclosure. Tests: 314 pass (18 new across rollup util + cache + PluginRail scope behaviour). Demoted from epic to feature pre-implementation — actual work was a single TDD pass.

title: Light mode + theme toggle
description:
## Problem / opportunity

The walking skeleton shipped dark-only. macOS users expect at minimum System auto-follow; many also work in light mode. Reintroducing light mode is also the forcing function to audit hard-coded colour values across component CSS modules — making the token system finally do its job.

## UX (locked)

**Tri-state toggle: System / Light / Dark** in the **View menu** of the native macOS menu, alongside future zoom-related items. macOS-standard convention. No settings panel for v1.

**Default: System** — auto-follows the OS appearance via `window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: light)")` and re-applies on change without a re-launch.

## Implementation strategy (locked)

- `:root` block in `src/styles/tokens.css` keeps the current dark values as the default.
- `:root[data-theme="light"]` block overrides every `--c-*` token with light values.
- A new `useThemeStore` (or a slice on the existing `useUIStore`) holds `theme: "system" | "light" | "dark"`. Sets the `data-theme` attribute on `documentElement`. For `system`, sets it based on `prefers-color-scheme` and listens for OS-level changes.
- Persisted via `src/lib/persistence.ts` — mirrors the `textZoom` pattern from `lpx-explorer-1kn` (`loadThemePreference` / `persistThemePreference`).
- View-menu items wire through the existing `menu-event` channel (same pattern as the Help-menu items in `lpx-explorer-5hf`).

## Light palette (starting point — refine in the tokenisation child bead)

Reference: Logic Pro 11 light mode + macOS system colours.

| Token | Dark | Light |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--c-bg` | `#1d1d1f` | `#f5f5f7` |
| `--c-surface` | `#2a2a2c` | `#ffffff` |
| `--c-surface-2` | `#323234` | `#ececec` |
| `--c-divider` | `#3a3a3c` | `#d2d2d7` |
| `--c-text` | `#f5f5f7` | `#1d1d1f` |
| `--c-text-secondary` | `rgba(245,245,247,0.7)` | `rgba(29,29,31,0.7)` |
| `--c-text-muted` | `rgba(245,245,247,0.5)` | `rgba(29,29,31,0.5)` |
| `--c-accent` | `#5e9eff` | `#5e9eff` (works in both) |

Status colours (`--c-status-clean / warn / fail`) keep their semantic hue — may need slight tonal lift in light mode.

## Audit pass — required before tokens land

`grep -rE "rgba\(|#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}" src/**/*.module.css` will surface every hard-coded colour. Known offenders that need new tokens before light overrides will work:

- `CompatibilityVerdict.module.css` — status-tinted band backgrounds (rgba per status)
- `Inspector.module.css` — `installBadge` tints
- `TrackRow.module.css` — kind-coloured pill backgrounds (`#3a8dde` for fx, plus rgba tints)
- `PluginRail.module.css` — install badges, highlight animation keyframes
- `EmptyState.module.css` — primary-button hover

Each of these needs a tokenised equivalent (e.g. `--c-status-clean-tint`) so the light theme can override.

## Decomposition (file these as child beads when implementation kicks off)

1. **Audit + tokenisation pass** — extract every hard-coded colour into a `--c-*` token. Pure refactor; no theme work yet. Acceptance: zero hex / rgba() literals in `src/**/*.module.css` outside `tokens.css`.
2. **Light-mode token block** — add `:root[data-theme="light"]` overrides. Pick Logic-Pro-light + macOS-system colours.
3. **Theme store + System follow** — `useThemeStore`; `data-theme` attribute sync on `documentElement`; `prefers-color-scheme` listener with cleanup.
4. **View menu toggle** — three native menu items (System / Light / Dark) routed through `menu-event`. Show a checkmark on the active option.
5. **Persistence** — extend the existing `tauri-plugin-store` library file with a `theme` key. Hydrate on mount.
6. **Visual QA** — open every screen (EmptyState, Inspector with project loaded, scanning, error, missing-rows, Klopfgeist row, expand-all, both rails, drop-hint, context menu) in both modes. Fix any regressions.

Each child bead links back via `bd dep add <child> sme`.

## Out of scope

- High-contrast / increased-contrast mode (separate epic if a user requests).
- Per-component theme overrides — single global theme.
- Animated transitions between themes — single hard cut on toggle (matches the verdict-band hard-cut policy from `lpx-explorer-o4w`).
- Custom themes / user-defined palettes.
- Sepia / solarized / other variants.

LABELS: ui-polish, epic
acceptance_criteria: Light-mode token block defined under :root[data-theme='light'] with semantic parity to the dark palette; useThemeStore drives the data-theme attribute; System mode auto-follows prefers-color-scheme and updates without re-launch; theme persists across launches via tauri-plugin-store; native View menu carries System / Light / Dark items with a checkmark on the active option; zero hex / rgba literals remain in src/**/*.module.css (tokenisation child bead); no visual regressions in dark mode (existing baseline); each surface looks correct in both modes (visual QA child bead).

title: Switch tlog! timestamp to HH:MM:SS.mmm wall-clock
description:
## Problem

The diagnostic logger currently prepends `[+Nms]` (millis since process start). Useful for triaging the cold-start gap, less useful day-to-day where you want to know *when* an event happened against the wall clock.

## Change

`tlog!` macro in `src-tauri/src/lib.rs`: prepend `[HH:MM:SS.mmm]` (local time, 24-hour) instead of `[+Nms]`. Keep everything else the same — the bridge in `dev-log.ts` doesn't need to change because it just forwards messages; Rust does the timestamping on receipt.

Drop the `APP_START` OnceLock + `elapsed_ms()` helper if nothing else uses it after this change.

## Implementation hint

`std::time::SystemTime::now()` → `chrono` is the easy path but adds a dep. Alternatively use `std::time` + manual hour/min/sec arithmetic against UNIX_EPOCH, then add the local-tz offset via `localtime_r` or a small helper. Pick whichever is cleanest.

## Acceptance

- Every `tlog!` line in the dev terminal starts with `[HH:MM:SS.mmm]` in local time.
- The `[+0ms] [main] start` first-line marker becomes `[HH:MM:SS.mmm] [main] start`.
- JS-bridged logs (`[js:level] [js+Nms] …`) still carry the `[js+Nms]` JS-relative timestamp internally — Rust just stamps the wall-clock on top.
- All cargo tests still pass.

## Out of scope

- A persistent log file. The terminal stream is the diagnostic surface; users grep it directly.

title: Plugin category v2 — fine-grained Logic-style categories (EQ, Dynamics, Reverb, …)
description:
## Background

lpx-explorer-01w shipped coarse type-based categorisation (Effects / Instruments / MIDI). The investigation pass revealed that fine-grained Logic-Pro-style categories (EQ, Dynamics, Distortion, Modulation, Delay, Reverb, Pitch, Imaging, Metering, Utility, Specialty, Drum Machine, Sampler) **aren't deterministically recoverable** from `.component` bundle Info.plists — only 2 of 226 bundles on the reference Mac even had a `tags` array and both were empty.

## Problem

A user looking at a project with 30+ inserts wants to slice by 'show me reverbs' or 'show me dynamics', not just 'show me effects'. The Effects chip from v1 narrows from ~40 plug-ins to ~30 — still too coarse.

## Approach options (pick one)

1. **Static fingerprint→category map.** Mirror the `STOCK_FINGERPRINTS` table from `apple_stock.rs`. Cover Apple stock plug-ins first (the well-known set), expand to common 3rd-party as desired. Accurate for known plug-ins, 'Uncategorised' for unknown.
2. **Display-name heuristics.** Regex `/(reverb|verb)/i` → Reverb; `/(comp|limiter|gate)/i` → Dynamics. Fast to implement, fragile, vendor-name-dependent.
3. **Hybrid** — static map for known + heuristics fallback for unknown. Best coverage, biggest maintenance surface.

Lean: **(1) static map**. Mirrors the established STOCK_FINGERPRINTS pattern; deterministic; no surprise miscategorisations.

## Proposed deliverable

- `lib/au-categories.ts` gains a `FINE_CATEGORIES` static table (`fingerprint → fine category string`).
- `categoryOfFingerprint` returns the fine category when known, falls back to coarse.
- New chip row OR replace the v1 chips with finer subdivisions (UX call to make).
- 'M of N categorised' indicator next to the rail count — meaningful now since unknowns are 'Uncategorised'.

## Out of scope

- Crowd-sourced category contributions.
- Per-instance category overrides.

title: Extend STOCK_FINGERPRINTS table for Bass Amp, Limiter, Phat FX, Graph EQ, ChromaGlow, Alchemy, Drummer, Bass Player
description:
Spawned from lpx-explorer-duj (2026-05-06). The static-fingerprint-lookup mechanism shipped, seeded with one verified entry (`Compressor` → `aufx/Comp/appl`). Names recovered from the repro project (`~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx`) but absent from the table:

- `Limiter`

- `Graph EQ`
- `ChromaGlow`
- `Alchemy`
- `Drummer`     (from apple_drummer scanner)
- `Bass Player` (from apple_drummer scanner)

These currently fall through to `synth_subtype` and are kept "installed" by the `display_name`-based fallback in `CompatibilityVerdict.countMissing` — the user-visible behaviour is correct, but the fingerprint diverges from `auval -l` output, so:
1. Cross-version-detection JTBDs (e.g. ChromaGlow ⇒ Logic 11+) are blocked.
2. A 4CC-format hit for the same plug-in won't dedupe against the GAME-format hit.

## Acceptance

Add a unit test asserting the round-trip fingerprint. Verify on the repro project that every recovered AURef has a fingerprint that appears in `auval -l`.

## Why it didn't ship in lpx-explorer-duj

This work session ran on a Mac where Logic Pro is installed but its stock plug-ins were not registered in the AU cache (auval -l returned only system CoreAudio AUs, no Logic-stock entries). title: Static fingerprint lookup table for Apple stock plug-ins
description:
Spawned from lpx-explorer-0wo (2026-05-06). The GAME-marker scanner introduced in 0wo recovers the display name of Apple stock plug-ins (Compressor, Limiter, Bass Amp, etc.) but synthesises a fake (type, subtype, manufacturer) fingerprint because the real one isn't recoverable from the binary format.

## Why this matters

The synthesised fingerprints (`aufx/comp/appl`, `aufx/bass/appl`, etc.) won't cross-reference against `auval -l` output. As a workaround, CompatibilityVerdict treats every AURef with display_name set as "always installed". That's safe for stock plug-ins on a Mac with Logic, but means we lose the ability to:

1. Detect when a project requires a Logic version that has the plug-in (e.g. ChromaGlow only exists in Logic 11+).
2. Surface the same plug-in fingerprint when the same plug-in is detected via 4CC vs GAME (currently they appear as duplicate-ish entries with different fingerprints).

## Implementation strategy

Build a static lookup table mapping Apple stock display name → real fingerprint. Two sources:
1. `auval -l` output on a stock-Logic install. List all `appl`-manufactured AUs; map their `name` field to the (type, subtype) tuple.
2. Apple's documentation for component subtypes (some are documented in CoreAudio headers).

Ship the table as data. When apple_stock::find_apple_stock_aus matches a known display name, use the real fingerprint instead of the synthesised one.

## Acceptance

For repro project, every Apple stock AU returned by find_aus has a fingerprint that matches an entry in `auval -l` output on a stock-Logic Mac. CompatibilityVerdict's display_name-based shortcut becomes unnecessary (or remains as a fallback for unknown stock plug-ins).
acceptance_criteria: Apple stock plug-ins detected via the GAME marker have fingerprints that match auval -l output; the display_name-based 'always installed' shortcut in CompatibilityVerdict becomes redundant for known plug-ins.
close_reason: Static lookup table mechanism shipped in apple_stock.rs (commit 7db2f6e). STOCK_FINGERPRINTS map keyed by display name; lookup_stock_fingerprint() returns the real auval (type, subtype) when known, falls through to synth_subtype otherwise. CompatibilityVerdict.countMissing now checks the registry first and uses the display_name shortcut as a fallback for unknown stock plug-ins. Seeded with Compressor → aufx/Comp/appl (verified against lpx-toolkit/tests/test_diagnostics.py). 256 vitest + 102 cargo tests pass. Extension to other recovered names (Bass Amp, Limiter, Phat FX, Graph EQ, ChromaGlow, Alchemy, Drummer, Bass Player) filed as lpx-explorer-d5f — requires Logic-launch-then-auval-l on a stock-Logic install, which this session's machine couldn't provide (Logic plug-ins were not registered in the AU cache).

title: Recover Apple Drummer / Bass Player AU via JSON state (Pattern 4)
description:
Spawned from lpx-explorer-0wo (2026-05-06). The 0wo bead recovered 12 of 13 expected AU descriptors via the GAME 4CC marker. The 1 still-missing AU is the Apple Drummer / Bass Player feature, which uses a different storage shape: embedded JSON state strings.

## What's missing

For repro project ~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx:
- Track 2 ("Bass") uses Logic's Drummer plug-in in Bass Player mode.
- Identified by JSON state at offset 0x1038A7 with key
  "selectedPersistentCharacterTypeIdentifier":"Type_ElectricBassV2"
  and "selectedCharacterIdentifier":"Electric Bass - Pop Songwriter".

## Implementation strategy

1. Scan raw bytes for `"persistentCharacterTypeIdentifier":"Type_` substring.
2. Walk forward to the closing `"`, capture the type identifier.
3. Map to AURef via static table (Type_ElectricBassV2 → Drummer plug-in fingerprint).
4. Synthesise display name from the identifier or use a static lookup.

15 occurrences of `selectedCharacterIdentifier` exist in the binary section (per spike). Need to dedupe by track / channel.

## Acceptance

For repro project, find_aus on ~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx returns 13 of 13 AU descriptors. The Drummer / Bass Player AU has an entry with display_name set. Cargo tests cover the JSON-state extraction with hand-crafted byte fixtures.

## Out of scope

- Static lookup table for ALL Apple Drummer characters (maintenance burden — only need the ones we encounter).
- General-purpose JSON parsing — the substring + walk-to-quote approach is sufficient.
acceptance_criteria: find_aus on ~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx returns 13 of 13 AU descriptors; the Drummer / Bass Player AU entry has display_name set; cargo tests cover the JSON-state extraction.
close_reason: Pattern 4 (Apple Drummer / Bass Player JSON state) implemented. Cluster heuristic by byte-offset proximity (32 KB threshold) collapses per-region snapshots to one AURef per Drummer instance. Static map for known character types (Type_AcousticDrummerV2 → 'Drummer', Type_ElectricBassV2 → 'Bass Player'); fallback to stripped Type_X for unknown chars. On repro project, find_aus returns exactly 13 of 13 AUs (was 12) — acceptance criterion met. Bass Player visible in the right rail; track-attachment to the correct chain row is a known offset-heuristic limitation that overlaps with lpx-explorer-nro.

title: Plug-in Chains rows show 'Inst N' instead of user-given track name
description:
Spawned from lpx-explorer-env (2026-05-06). The "Tracks" section (`<TrackRegistry>`) now correctly displays user-given track names like `Piano`, `Bass`, `Luscious Arp Layers`. But the sibling "Plug-in Chains" section (`<TrackList>`) still shows channel-strip auto names like `Inst 1`, `Inst 2` for the same tracks. The user-given name is in the parser output — it's just on the wrong list.

## What you see today

For `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx` (after env's fix):

| Plug-in Chains row | Should display |
|---|---|
| Audio 1 | (no rename — keep) |
| Inst 1 | Piano |
| Inst 2 | Bass |
| Inst 3 | Luscious Arp Layers |
| Inst 4 | Drums |
| Inst 5 | Untitled (no rename — keep) |
| Inst 6 | UnexpectedlyNamedTrack |

## Why the gap exists

Two parallel scanners produce two parallel lists:

- `find_tracks` (`tracks.rs`) emits `Track` records keyed by channel-strip-record byte offset. Field `user_name: Option<String>`. Today only `assign_user_names` fills it — and only from `RegionCluster` (i.e. the names of recorded regions). Tracks without recorded regions stay `None`.
- `find_track_registry_records` (`tracks_registry.rs`) emits `TrackRegistryEntry` records keyed by registry-record byte offset. Carries `track_id` (uint16 LE at offset -62) and `strip_id` (uint16 LE in the audio-track trailer). Has the user-given name. Lives in `ProjectSummary.tracks_registry` — the data the "Tracks" UI section reads.

The two lists describe the same logical tracks but use **different byte ranges** with no shared key on the `Track` side. The join from registry → channel-strip is unsolved.

## Join hypotheses to investigate

1. **Audio tracks via `strip_id`**: registry trailer encodes `uint16 LE` = strip number. Channel-strip descriptors may encode the same number — `descriptor[4]` is documented as "alternate activity signal" but may also be the strip number. Worth a hex-diff between two audio tracks with known different strip numbers.

2. **Instrument tracks via `track_id`**: registry preamble encodes `uint16 LE` track ID at offset -62. lpx-toolkit/CLAUDE.md ("Per-track ID: SOLVED") says these IDs are stable and globally unique. Question: does the channel-strip record contain or sit adjacent to the same track ID? If yes, surface it on `Track`; if no, find another correlation.

3. **Fallback heuristic** if neither byte-level join works: order-based pairing. Pair registry entries (filtered to user-renamed only) with channel strips of the same `TrackKind` in some canonical order. Risky — earlier in this project I observed that channel-strip storage order doesn't match Logic-UI track-row order, so naive offset-asc pairing got Bass/Drums swapped.

## Implementation strategy

1. **Spike** (1-2 h): hex-diff two minimal projects to nail down the channel-strip → registry join. Outcome is a documented byte offset + decoder function.
2. **Surface the join key on `Track`**: add `track_id: Option<u16>` and/or `strip_id: Option<u16>` fields. Populated by `find_tracks`.
3. **New join function** `assign_registry_names(&mut [Track], &[TrackRegistryEntry])`: fills `user_name` for tracks where it's still `None`, joining by track_id/strip_id.
4. **Wire into `parse_project`** after `assign_user_names`.
5. **`<TrackRow>` rendering**: already prefers `user_name` via `track-display.ts:19-21` — no UI change needed. The fix is purely upstream.

## Out of scope

- Tracks with regions: already covered by `assign_user_names` from clusters.
- Apple stock plug-in identity: separate gap, lpx-explorer-0wo.
- Channel-strip-side reverse engineering of UI row order: separate concern.

## Acceptance criteria

For `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx`, "Plug-in Chains" rows for Inst 1, Inst 2, Inst 3, Inst 4, Inst 6 display Piano, Bass, Luscious Arp Layers, Drums, UnexpectedlyNamedTrack respectively. Inst 5 (genuinely Untitled) and Audio 1 (phantom default strip) keep their existing names. Cargo tests cover the join. No regression on tracks recovered via cluster_regions.
acceptance_criteria: For ~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx, Plug-in Chains rows for Inst 1, Inst 2, Inst 3, Inst 4, Inst 6 display Piano, Bass, Luscious Arp Layers, Drums, UnexpectedlyNamedTrack respectively. Inst 5 (genuinely Untitled) and Audio 1 (phantom default strip) keep their existing names. Cargo tests cover the join. No regression on tracks recovered via cluster_regions.
close_reason: Ordinal pairing within kind by offset order. New assign_registry_names function pairs the Nth instrument-kind registry entry (sorted by offset) with the Nth instrument-kind active channel strip (sorted by offset), and similarly for audio. Removed 'Untitled' from REGISTRY_NOISE so the count matches channel-strip records 1:1 (an unrenamed instrument track IS labelled 'Untitled' in Logic's UI, so the registry record carries real user-facing intent). On the repro project, all 6 instrument strips display the correct user name: Piano, Luscious Arp Layers, Bass, Drums, Untitled, UnexpectedlyNamedTrack. Manual UI verification on ~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx confirmed. The byte-level join (registry track_id → channel-strip) is genuinely unsolved upstream (lpx-toolkit/CLAUDE.md 'UI track-row order: STRUCTURE FOUND, encoding partially reverse-engineered'); ordinal pairing ships as the working approximation. No regression on tracks recovered via cluster_regions — assign_registry_names doesn't overwrite a non-None user_name.

title: Insights v1 — library plugin frequency bar chart
description:
New top-level 'Insights' route alongside the per-project Inspector. v1 is a single visualisation answering one library-level question: 'Which plug-ins do I actually use across my whole library?'

WALKING-SKELETON SLICE (this bead):
Horizontal bar chart of the top 20 plug-ins across all scanned .logicx
projects in the user's library, ranked by *project count* (used in
47/120 projects), not instance count. Project count is more useful for

title: Inline name filter for Tracks + Plug-in Chains sections
description:
## Problem/Opportunity
Even after the Inspector IA reorg (lpx-explorer-fom) lands collapse-by-default for track inserts and a rail-side plug-in filter, the main-column Tracks and Plug-in Chains sections still lack a name filter. On 80+ track projects the user can't quickly answer 'where's the Bass track?' without scrolling.

This bead narrows the original 'navigability' framing to the unambiguous remaining slice: the inline track-name filter (option (a) from the original three design candidates). Options (b) collapse inserts and (c) independent scroll have been folded into 'fom' as part of the IA reorg.

## Proposed Solution
Small search input in each section's header (Tracks + Plug-in Chains). Mirrors the LibraryRail's existing LibrarySearch pattern. Filters visible rows by track name in real time, case-insensitive substring match against `track.user_name ?? track.name`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Search input renders in the section header for both Tracks (TrackRegistry) and Plug-in Chains (TrackList).
- [ ] Typing narrows the visible rows in real time (debounced if needed for >200 row projects).
- [ ] Empty query restores the full list.
- [ ] Match is case-insensitive substring on `user_name` (preferred) with `name` fallback.
- [ ] Filter is per-section: filtering one section does NOT affect the other, the rail's PluginList, or coverage indicators.
- [ ] Filter input visually consistent with LibrarySearch (reuse if practical).
- [ ] Empty-state placeholder when filter has no matches: 'No tracks match "<query>".'

## Out of Scope
- Plug-in name filtering (handled by lpx-explorer-fom's rail filter).
- Filtering by AU type/category (handled by lpx-explorer-01w's category chips once that ships).
- Persistent filter state across project switches or app launches.
- Multi-token / regex / fuzzy matching — substring is enough for v1.

## Notes
- Loose dependency on `fom`: ships independently, but reads cleanest after `fom` since collapse-by-default makes the filter feel additive rather than compensatory. Reassess whether this is still needed if `fom` alone relieves the pressure.
- Repro project: any Logic project with 50+ user-visible channel strips. The user has at least one on hand.
- Original framing (filed 2026-05-05) was a P2 'navigability' epic. Narrowed to a small, additive improvement after the IA reorg captured the structural changes.
acceptance_criteria: Search input in both Tracks and Plug-in Chains headers narrows the section's visible rows by case-insensitive substring on user_name (or name fallback) in real time; filters are per-section and don't affect the rail or coverage indicators; empty-state when no matches; visually consistent with LibrarySearch.

title: NSKeyedArchive parser — unlocks track renames + Apple stock plugin coverage
description:
Today's coverage:
  - Audio tracks WITH recorded regions: user_name recovered from cluster_regions (lpx-explorer-qib).
  - Instrument tracks: user_name falls back to the loaded AU display name (lpx-explorer-59o).
  - Auto-named clusters skipped so user renames win (commit 0753e5c).

Gap that remains: audio tracks the user has renamed but never recorded into. The user-given name lives in NSKeyedArchive (bplist00) blobs spliced into ProjectData, not in any region record or channel-strip record. Per lpx-toolkit/CLAUDE.md "How the parsing actually works": "NSKeyedArchive blobs ... are the path to richer extraction (track->plugin mapping, parameter values, full plugin names) and represent the next major piece of work."

The Python tool ALSO shows "Audio N" for these tracks - the format is not reverse-engineered there either. Confirmed in smoke test 2026-05-05.

Implementation strategy when this is picked up:
  1. Find bplist00 magic bytes in ProjectData.
  2. Walk forward to the 32-byte trailer (find_bplist_end exists in Python - port it).
  3. Parse via the plist crate (already a dep; handles binary plists).
  4. Extract track-related fields (NSKey-archive Cocoa objects).
  5. Cross-reference with find_tracks output.

Multi-day reverse-engineering effort - explicitly out of scope until a real-world need motivates it.
design:
# Implementation plan (Software Architect, 2026-05-06)

## Critical premise to verify first

`lpx-toolkit/lpx_inspect.py:1314-1326` is explicit that the Python author looked inside bplists and concluded user-facing track names do NOT live there (Smart Controls layouts, parameter mappings, channel UUIDs, automation — yes; track names — no). That contradicts this bead's headline assumption. **A go/no-go spike (`lpx-explorer-<spike-id>`) gates all implementation work.**

If the spike returns:
- Q1=no, Q2=yes — drop track-renames; rewrite this bead as "Apple stock plug-in coverage via NSKeyedArchive".
- Q1=yes, Q2=no — keep gap #1 only; spawn separate bead for stock plug-ins.
- Q1=no, Q2=no — premise wrong; close this bead and re-investigate from raw bytes.
- Q1=yes, Q2=yes — proceed to slice 1.

## Architecture: single-pass scan, two extractors

```
src-tauri/crates/lpx-parser/src/
  bplist.rs          # scan_blobs: find magic + walk 32-byte trailer + plist::from_bytes
  bplist_archive.rs  # NSKeyedArchive object-graph resolver (port of resolve_archive)
  bplist_renames.rs  # extractor: track names
  bplist_aus.rs      # extractor: stock-plug-in AU descriptors
```

One `scan_blobs` produces an IR; per-gap extractors consume it. Splitting raw scan from Cocoa-graph traversal lets the scanner be tested against ordinary bplists (no NSKeyedArchive wrapper needed).

## Join key: byte-offset proximity (no new logic needed)

`assign_user_names` (`tracks.rs:74-86`) and `assign_aus` (`tracks.rs:99-117`) already join evidence to tracks via "nearest preceding track by offset". Bplist-derived evidence inherits `anchor_offset = blob.start` and reuses the existing assignment passes.

Backup: channel-UUID (`_WsChannelUUID`) join — only if the offset heuristic is shown to fail on the repro project. Separate bead.

## Vertical slices (after spike returns Q1=yes, Q2=yes)

| # | Slice | Estimate | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Spike on `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx` | 2-4 h | bd comment with Q1/Q2/Q3 answers |
| 1 | Tracer: one rename end-to-end (RED test → minimal scanner + resolver + extractor + wire-up) | 4-6 h | `cargo test` + manual UI check |
| 2 | Manual real-fixture proof on repro project | 30 min | screenshot in bd |
| 3 | Anonymised Layer-B fixture + test | 3-5 h | `cargo test` |
| 4 | Stock-AU extractor (instrument: Bass, Alchemy) | 4-6 h | `cargo test` + manual UI |
| 5 | Stock-AU extractor (audio FX, MIDI FX) | 3-5 h | `cargo test` + manual UI |
| 6 | Fail-safe tests (truncated, corrupted, zero-blob, read-only invariant) | 2 h | `cargo test` |
| 7 | Docs + decision-log entries + spawn follow-up beads | 1 h | bd close |

Total ~20-30 h, consistent with the "multi-day reverse-engineering effort" note.

## Test fixtures (three layers)

- **Layer A — hand-built minimal NSKeyedArchive blobs**: written via `plist` crate's binary writer (`tests/fixtures/build_archive.rs`). Verifies scanner + resolver mechanics. Cheap, low-fidelity.
- **Layer B — anonymised real blobs from repro project**: extract a real blob, walk graph, replace sensitive NSStrings with same-length placeholders, re-serialise. Commit as `tests/fixtures/bplist/*.bplist` with provenance `.md` sibling. Load-bearing — exercises actual Logic encoding.
- **Layer C — `ProjectData`-shaped composites**: Layer B blobs interleaved with 4CC-anchored noise. Tests scanner under realistic false-positive density.

**Never** commit unmodified `.logicx` blobs. Add a pre-commit linter on `tests/fixtures/bplist/` that rejects strings matching obvious PII patterns (`~/Music/Logic/`, user name, etc.).

## Risks

| # | Risk | Could kill bead? | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Track names not in bplists | Yes (rewrites bead) | Spike Q1 |
| 2 | AU descriptors as Cocoa class graphs not raw 4CCs | No (changes extractor shape) | Spike Q2 |
| 3 | Trailer-walker O(n²) on pathological inputs | No | Bound `max_end` per Python; perf test on repro project |
| 4 | `plist` crate doesn't write binary | No | Confirmed default features include writer |
| 5 | Offset-join heuristic wrong | Possibly | Slice 2 manual gate; escalates to UUID join (separate bead) |
| 6 | PII slips into Layer-B fixture | No | Anonymisation procedure + pre-commit linter |
| 7 | Truncated/corrupted blobs in the wild | No | Slice 6 fail-safes |
| 8 | Logic versions emit different NSKeyedArchive shapes | No (acknowledged) | Mark "partially solved" in CLAUDE.md per AC |

## Scope guardrails

**In scope**: scanner, NSKeyedArchive resolver, track-rename extractor, stock-AU extractor (`aumu`/`aufx`/`aumf` with `appl` and any other manufacturer codes seen on repro project), offset-join wire-up, three-layer test fixtures, `lpx-toolkit/CLAUDE.md` update.

**Out of scope — spawn follow-up beads when this closes**:
- Plug-in parameter values (knob positions, A/B states)
- Full plug-in display names beyond `auval -l` lookup
- Smart Controls metadata (`contentTagLayoutName`, knob labels)
- Channel-UUID-based join key (only if offset heuristic fails)
- Automation curve points (`MAGraphPoint`)
- PyO3 bindings so `lpx-toolkit` consumes the Rust bplist parser

## Decisions to log in `docs/decisions.md`

1. bplist parser: native Rust port using `plist` crate + hand-rolled scanner + NSKeyedArchive resolver (no fork/vendor of `plist`).
2. Single-pass scan with two extractors (rejected: per-gap scans).
3. Join key: blob start offset (rejected: `_WsChannelUUID`-based join, deferred).
4. Test fixtures: hand-rolled + anonymised real blobs, no raw user data committed; pre-commit PII linter on fixture dir.
5. Scope cap: track names + stock-plug-in AU descriptors only; spawn beads for parameters, Smart Controls, automation.

## Done definition

**Tests** (Rust):
- `bplist::tests::scans_single_blob_at_known_offset` (Layer A)
- `bplist::tests::handles_truncated_trailer` (Layer A)
- `bplist::tests::skips_blob_with_invalid_trailer_continues_to_next` (Layer C)
- `bplist_archive::tests::resolves_nsstring_to_native_string` (Layer A)
- `bplist_archive::tests::resolves_nested_nsdictionary` (Layer A)
- `bplist_renames::tests::extracts_name_from_anonymised_real_blob` (Layer B)
- `bplist_aus::tests::extracts_apple_stock_instrument_from_anonymised_blob` (Layer B)
- `bplist_aus::tests::extracts_apple_stock_audio_fx_from_anonymised_blob` (Layer B)
- Existing `test_readonly_invariant.rs` still GREEN.

**`<TrackList>` on `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx`**:
- Bass track shows "Bass" (Apple stock) instead of nothing.
- Luscious Arp Layers shows "Alchemy" instead of nothing.
- At least one of the six stock audio FX on Bass surfaces in the UI.
- Two `Untitled` tracks: render true rename (or confirm "Untitled" is genuine).
- No regression vs. pre-bead screenshot.

**`lpx-toolkit/CLAUDE.md`** — update the NSKeyedArchive section (lines ~17, ~213) from "next major piece of work" to "**Partially solved (2026-MM-DD)** — Rust port at `lpx-explorer/src-tauri/crates/lpx-parser/src/bplist*.rs`. The long tail (parameter values, Smart Controls metadata, full plug-in display names, automation curves) remains open."

**Quality gates green**: `cargo test`, `npm run quality`, pre-commit hooks. `cargo test` includes a perf assertion (e.g. <200 ms scan of repro project's `ProjectData`).

**Beads filed for spawned work** before close.

## Files referenced

- `src-tauri/crates/lpx-parser/src/{lib,tracks,tracks_registry}.rs`
- `src-tauri/crates/lpx-parser/Cargo.toml` (confirms `plist = "1"`)
- `src-tauri/src/commands.rs` (wire-up site)
- `src/lib/{types,track-display}.ts`
- `src/components/Inspector/TrackList.tsx`
- `docs/decisions.md`
- `/Users/rhyd/code/lpx-toolkit/lpx_inspect.py` lines 1304-1488 (`find_bplist_end`, `extract_bplists`, `resolve_archive`, `summarise_bplists`)
- `/Users/rhyd/code/lpx-toolkit/CLAUDE.md` lines 17, 213 (update target)

Logic ground truth (6 tracks):

  2. Bass (Bass), 6 audio FX, 0 MIDI FX

# Spike result (2026-05-06) — Q1=NO, Q2=NO

Ran a Python diagnostic against `~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx/Alternatives/000/ProjectData` (1,061,235 bytes) reusing `lpx_inspect.py`'s already-working `extract_bplists` and `resolve_archive`. Three phases: full graph traversal, raw `$objects` enumeration of every `WsPluginIdentity` instance, exhaustive search for AU-4CC integers/strings/bytes anywhere in any bplist.

## Q1 — track names in bplists: **NO**

Searched every resolved bplist graph for the strings `'Bass'`, `'Piano'`, `'Drums'`, `'Luscious Arp Layers'`, `'Untitled'` — the user-given names from the Logic ground truth in lpx-explorer-14d Notes.

**Zero hits.** Sample of strings actually present (Smart Controls and articulation labels):

```
'Monsters Inc (Acapella 110 bpm) Natali Noor'   ← project title (only)
'Automatic-Modern Synth 8 Single Row'
'Studio Bass Finger.plist'                       ← sampler patch filename
'MAPlugInParameterMapping'
'Dead Note Harmonics Index'
'Slide by Velocity'
'_WsChannelUUID'
'Tonal Balance'
'High Shelf' / 'Low Shelf' / 'Mid Freq' / 'Predelay' / 'LPF/HPF' / 'Reverb' / 'Chorus'
```

These are Smart Controls layouts and EQ/articulation labels — exactly what `lpx_inspect.py:1314-1326` already documented bplists contain.

## Q2 — Apple stock-AU integer triples in bplists: **NO**

Searched for `(componentType, componentSubType, componentManufacturer)` keyed triples under three plausible key-name schemes — zero matches.

Then exhaustively scanned every integer in every `$objects` array across all 30 blobs for values that decode as big-endian uint32 to known AU 4CCs (`aumu`/`aufx`/`aumf`/`aumi`/`appl`/`Appl`/`Toon`/`Artu`/`Bass`/`Alch`/`EZk2`/`EZd3`/`Kat1`):

```
## AU 4CCs found as integers: 0 hit(s)
## AU 4CCs found as 4-byte strings: 0 hit(s)
## AU 4CCs found as bytes: 4 hit(s)
    2× 'Appl(in-bytes)'
    2× 'appl(in-bytes)'
```

The four bytes hits are substrings inside larger byte blobs (UTI strings / class identifiers like `com.apple.…`), not structured AU descriptors. Consistent with the bead's Notes ("'appl' (raw): 9 occurrences (none adjacent to AU markers)").

**Apple stock plug-in identity is NOT stored in NSKeyedArchive blobs.** Whatever the parser is missing for Bass instrument / Alchemy / audio FX / MIDI FX, it's somewhere else in `ProjectData` (or possibly in a different file in the bundle entirely).

## Q3 — blob inventory

- 30 `bplist00` blobs successfully parsed (one — blob 10 — has no `$top` and resolve fails, but extracts).
- Largest blob: 8,665 bytes; smallest: 60 bytes; median: 1,514 bytes.
- Total bplist payload: 80,322 bytes (7.6% of `ProjectData`).
- Perf budget for the eventual scanner port: trivial. Even worst-case `O(n²)` trailer-walking finishes in well under 200 ms on this file.

## $classname distribution (top, across all blobs)

```
29 NSMutableDictionary   (generic)
 9 WsPluginIdentity      ← MISLEADING NAME — see below
 8 NSMutableArray
 6 NSDictionary
 4 NSArray
 4 MAGraphPoint                ← automation curve points
 4 MAPlugInParameterMapping    ← Smart Controls → plug-in parameter mapping
 3 _WsChannelUUID              ← channel UUID (potential join key)
 3 NSAttributedString
 3 MAKeyboardLayer
 2 NSColorSpace / NSColor / NSMutableString
```

**`WsPluginIdentity` is not what its name suggests.** Phase-2 dump of all 33+33 instances across two large blobs shows it's the identity of Smart Controls UI elements:

```
$objects[7]:  uuidString → 'Smart Knob 8',    autogenerated: False
$objects[10]: uuidString → 'Smart LED 4',     autogenerated: False
$objects[14]: uuidString → 'Smart Button 3',  autogenerated: False
$objects[22]: uuidString → 'Smart Text 1',    autogenerated: False
... (Smart Knob 1-11, Smart Button 1-3, Smart LED 4-5, Smart Text 1-3)
```

Two fields only: `uuidString` and `autogenerated`. No reference to AU identity. The "Plugin" in the class name refers to Logic's Smart-Controls UI plug-in, not audio plug-ins.

## Outcome and recommended path

Per the spike's outcome guide in lpx-explorer-3iv:

> **Q1=no, Q2=no** → premise wrong. Close 14d. Spawn investigation bead from raw bytes.

The bead lpx-explorer-14d as filed has the wrong solution. The bplist parser does not unlock either gap. Both must be re-investigated against the binary section of `ProjectData`.

**Recommended next steps:**

1. **Close lpx-explorer-14d** with reason "premise wrong — see lpx-explorer-3iv spike"; do not implement the NSKeyedArchive parser as scoped.
2. **File new bead** for renamed-but-unrecorded audio track names: investigate where these names live in the binary section. The repro project is the same (`~/Music/Logic/ new idea.logicx`), and the four detected tracks-with-regions already work via cluster_regions, so the gap is narrow — just the silent renamed audio tracks. Hypothesis to try: the channel-strip record itself carries an inline name field that today's parser doesn't read, or there's an adjacent record signature we haven't identified.
3. **File new bead** for Apple stock plug-ins: investigate the binary section for non-4CC plug-in identifiers. Known clues from this spike: `MAPlugInParameterMapping` blobs reference plug-in parameters by index (so Logic *does* track which plug-ins are loaded at the bplist level — but only as parameter targets, with no manufacturer/type/subtype stored). The identity must therefore live in the binary section in a different shape than today's `find_aus` scanner expects. Possibly as a fixed-position field within the channel-strip record.
4. **Optional bead** — extract Smart Controls metadata as enrichment: the bplists *do* contain useful information (`contentTagLayoutName`, parameter mappings, channel UUIDs) that could enrich the inspector view. This is a real but separate feature, not what 14d asked for. Lower priority than the actual gaps.

## Diagnostic scripts

Three throwaway Python scripts in `/tmp/` (NOT committed): `bplist_spike.py`, `bplist_spike2.py`, `bplist_spike3.py`. Output preserved at `/tmp/bplist_spike{,2,3}.out` for one session — discard after this comment lands.

title: AU scan progress: ensure scanning state is visibly displayed
description:
Smoke test 2026-05-05: user reported the 'Scanning installed AUs… (N)' state was hard to see — the scan completed correctly but the live count never visibly climbed.

Likely causes:
1. Small AU library on the test machine (e.g. Apple defaults only ~50 entries) → scan completes in <500ms.
2. React 18 batching: dozens of setStatus calls within a single JS task collapse into a single render, so the count jumps from 0 to N rather than climbing.

Investigate options:
- Throttle the count updates to ~20 fps (setTimeout-based batching in the store's onEntry callback).
- Add a minimum-display time (e.g. 800ms) for the scanning state before transitioning to loaded.
- Add a CSS pulse animation on the pill while scanning so even an instant state is perceptible.

Lean: throttle onEntry to ~50ms intervals via a useDebounceEffect-style helper. Keeps the state machine honest while ensuring the user sees movement. Min-display-time is a smell (artificial delay).
acceptance_criteria: Scanning state is visibly perceptible to a human even on a system with <100 AUs; verdict transition feels intentional, not abrupt.
